#1886. What Sebastien Pocognoli said to Billy Gilmour after Scotland miss left him ‘alone on the pitch’

Sebastien Pocognoli has hailed the way Billy Gilmour responded to the horror of missing an open goal just moments after half-time against North Macedonia.

The midfielder experienced a moment to forget when he blazed over from the edge of the six-yard box with the goal gaping in front of him during Friday’s 2-1 Nations League win.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

All’s well that ended well as Scotland kept their Nations League hopes alive thanks to John McGinn’s double. However, there was concern when North Macedonia equalised almost immediately after the midfielder’s opener on 54 minutes.

Gilmour played his part in the recovery before being replaced by Ryan Christie two minutes after McGinn’s winner from the penalty spot. He was given a tremendous ovation by the home crowd, who recognised his bravery in playing through the difficult moments directly after the miss.

Gilmour had to literally pick himself back up from the turf after slumping to the ground following his moment to forget. Pocognoli noted “the noise” as fans sought to process what had happened. He described Gilmour as “alone on the pitch” in this period. But the midfielder did not hide and contributed to Scotland’s win.

McGinn’s second of the night from the spot, after Ben Gannon-Doak was tripped by goalkeeper Stole Dimitrievski, drew the midfielder level with Hughie Gallacher in third place in the all-time Scotland goalscorer standings with 24 goals.

Gilmour, who has scored twice in 51 international appearances, won’t ever feature at the top end of this list but he should now be sitting on three goals for Scotland.

Some have compared his miss to the infamous one suffered by striker Chris Iwelumo in a World Cup qualifier against Norway in 2008.

Peter van Vossen, whose name is forever associated with a horrendous open goal gaffe for Rangers against Celtic in a league fixture 30 years ago this weekend, was also referenced.

“For me, it is part of football to miss big chances,” said Pocognoli. “With his quality, he absolutely has to put it away. It was more difficult to put out!

“But I always say to the players that I am watching the reaction more. I was straight on at him after he missed. I say: ‘Go on!’ He reacted really well and I was really happy.

“That was what I said to him when he came off. I said: ‘Good reaction.’ Because there was a lot of noise after that and he was alone on the pitch. I think he did really well.”

#1885. GdS: Club Brugge name price for Tresoldi – why a difficult negotiation beckons for Milan

AC Milan have already discovered the starting price for Nicolo Tresoldi, and it’s safe to say it will not be a cheap deal.

According to this morning’s edition of La Gazzetta dello Sport (seen below), it is no secret that Tresoldi sits at the top of the wish list for Milan. Gerry Cardinale, first and foremost, is a big admirer of the rising Brugge star.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is equally well-known that the striker has been a lifelong fan of the Rossoneri. However, his contract runs until 2029, so to take him away from the Jan Breydel Stadium a negotiation is needed with a club that are tough to deal with, as the past shows.

The phone lines between Milan and Brugge were first used in 2022, when the Charles De Ketelaere saga took place. Since then, the management teams at both Milan and the Belgian club have changed, but the history between the two sides should help facilitate discussions. Ardon Jashari was another arduous negotiation, but one that eventually reached the finish line too.

In the cases of De Ketelaere and Jashari, the pitch has arguably favoured the seller more than the buyer. Perhaps the outcome will be different with Tresoldi, should the two parties actually sit down to negotiate.

One caveat: especially in January, the asking is bound to be significant. How significant? Around €60m, according to whispers from Flanders.

Club Brugge are accustomed to selling their best players when the time comes, but they are under no pressure to do so, especially while the season is still underway. Tresoldi has effectively carried the team on his back, scoring eight goals in the league, five in the Champions League, and one in the Super Cup.

The total: 14 goals in 17 official matches. For the club to part ways with their star striker during the mid-season window – a time when all their competitive objectives remain within reach – the offer would certainly need to be more than substantial.

Furthermore, if the 22-year-old forward maintains his current scoring rate throughout the season, his market value will only continue to climb. It is a risk, but also an opportunity. Moreover, Milan are not alone in the race for Tresoldi.

Bayern Munich and top English clubs are keeping a close eye on the former Hannover man, who was born in Cagliari but is a key player for the German U21 national team. Consequently, if Cardinale wishes to beat the competition, he would need to act quickly and decisively.

Tresoldi’s arrival could not see him then become a back-up to Gonçalo Ramos, the most expensive signing in the club’s history. In essence, it requires Ruben Amorim to provide the necessary assurances regarding the wisdom of the acquisition.

Meanwhile, Tresoldi’s hat-trick against Inter at San Siro on October 13th in the Champions League has naturally excited the Rossoneri fans, who would be more than happy to embrace him. However, they aren’t the ones who have to pay the €60m.

#1884. Michael Carrick issues first statement after Manchester United sacking

Michael Carrick has thanked Manchester United’s players and supporters following his sacking and insists he wants ‘nothing but success’ for the club.

Carrick was sacked by United on Thursday, while Mauricio Pochettino was officially announced as his replacement on Friday afternoon.

The 45-year-old returned to United in January following Ruben Amorim’s departure and joined on an interim deal until the end of last season.

Carrick was then rewarded with a two-year contract in May following United’s impressive end to the Premier League campaign, with no club in the top flight securing more points than the 36 United collected following Carrick’s arrival.

However, United have made a poor start to this season, registering just one win in 10 Premier League games – a run of results which has left the team 18th in the table.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Carrick retained the backing from United’s supporters, who have heavily booed the players during their dismal run of form, but the club’s hierarchy have opted to make a change by bringing in Pochettino.

In his statement which was released on Friday, Carrick wrote: ‘I’ve had the immense privilege of leading Manchester United, the football club that I love.

‘There are very few who get to live that and feel it, and for that I’m incredibly grateful.

‘With that comes huge responsibility, and to be at Manchester United, you need to understand exactly what that means. It’s different to anywhere else.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Ultimately, you need to push to be the best, but there is a culture, there are values and there are behaviours that you have to live by and respect, which have been built over a long period of time.

‘It’s a football club that is unique, with substance and history that cannot be ignored. This is what inspired me every single day.

‘I want to say a big thank you to the supporters. I must say, you are a special, rare breed.

‘We’ve had some great times this year and moments we’ll all remember. The best thing about being in my position was seeing so many of you lose yourselves in the emotion of those moments, leaving the stadium desperate to come back again next time.

‘I just wanted to give you something back. That love never dies.

‘I know we’ve not had the results lately, but you’ve shown me nothing but love and support in times when the easiest thing, and what most end up doing, would be to turn the other way.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

‘That means more than a win or two. That’s what makes you who you are.That’s why I fell in love with this club all those years ago.

‘A special thank you to my coaching staff. You gave me everything you had, every single day, and I couldn’t have asked for any more. I’m incredibly grateful for your loyalty, hard work and support throughout. To all the staff behind the scenes, thank you for everything you do for this football club. So much of your work goes unseen, but it never goes unappreciated.

‘And to the players, thank you for your efforts and the moments we’ve shared. I wish you all the very best for what’s ahead.

‘I want nothing but success for Manchester United. This club has been such a big part of my life and that will never change. I’ll always be proud to have played my part and I’ll always want the very best for it. I’ll be right there with you from now on, watching from the sidelines, cheering the lads on.’

#1882. Steyning’s second-half storm sinks Hastings United

The Barrowmen travelled full of confidence following their 2–1 home win over Horley Town. Hastings, meanwhile, were looking to respond after just one win in their previous four games, although a strong start to the league campaign meant they remained in the top three.

A crowd of 1,034 watched on a cold Saturday afternoon as an evenly contested opening offered few clear-cut chances.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Hastings broke the deadlock in the 20th minute when a corner caused chaos in the Steyning penalty area, with the ball going in off Conrad Honore for an own goal.

Chances remained scarce for the rest of the half as both sides defended well, allowing the hosts to take a slender advantage into the interval.

Steyning came flying out of the blocks after the restart and needed just four minutes to draw level, with Alex Brewer powering home a superb header.

Brewer struck again only a couple of minutes later, finishing off a fine Barrowmen counter-attack to turn the match on its head and put the visitors 2–1 ahead.

Charlie Pitcher extended Steyning’s lead on the hour mark, latching on to a well-judged headed flick-on to make it 3–1 and give the Barrowmen a two-goal cushion.

There was also an away debut from the bench for new signing Tosin Dada, whose arrival from Billingshurst had been announced late on Friday night.

Hastings threatened to pull a goal back, but Steyning goalkeeper Alfie Mansell produced a superb save, diving to his left.

Jesse Sentamu then rounded off an outstanding second-half display in the 90th minute, slotting past Harry Haines to make it 4–1 and ensure the Barrowmen headed home with all three points.

The victory lifts Steyning to 13th in the league table, while Hastings drop to fourth.

Both sides return to league action on Saturday – Steyning host Punjab while Hastings travel to Broadbridge Heath.

#1880. I watched Scotland’s World Cup games in the pub - but 142-day whirlwind has me primed to make Hampden impact

From watching the World Cup from the comfort of his local pub to making his first international start at the heart of Scotland’s defence, it’s been a remarkable couple of months for Luke Graham.

Nominated for the SWFA Young Player of the Year award following a series of colossal displays for Dundee last season, many tipped him to make a late claim for a place in Steve Clarke’s squad for the tournament in the summer. Despite coming close to making the final 26-man list, there was no seat on the plane for Graham.

Get our daily football newsletter by clicking here.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Courted by both Celtic and Rangers in the weeks that followed, Portsmouth had launched a seven-figure bid during the January window. However, when the summer transfer window re-opened, it was Stoke City who won the race for his signature. Currently third in the EFL Championship, Graham has been a star performer for them this season.

Awarded his first international start in Friday’s 2-1 win over North Macedonia, Graham admits things are beginning to fall into place. “Not much is going wrong for me at the moment,” he smiled. “I wouldn’t say I merited a start, we have a lot of good players in the camp. It’s up to the manager to pick the team and, luckily, he gave me the chance.

“I have to be ready for it. It’s something I’ve always wanted to do since I was growing up. It was a dream come true. I’ve always said that one thing I wanted to do in my career was play for Scotland, so to get it over the line was pretty special. I had my mum, my dad, my sister here and quite a few of my mates. A good turn out.

“We have a lot of good centre-halves. Obviously it was unfortunate for Welshy [Stephen Welsh] and Binksy [Luis Binks] to go out with injury but that opens up a space for me to come in and try to cement a place. When you’re out on that pitch, you have to do everything you can to try and stay in the team. I gave my all and I’ll just need to wait and see what happens.

“We’re going through a bit of a transitional spell just at the minute, so it’s not going to be all smooth sailing from the get-go. It’s about adjusting to that and try to build on performances in every game.”

It was all so different for the youngster a mere 142 days ago. Asked how he digested Scotland’s World Cup adventure - the first in his lifetime - during the summer, Graham’s financial situation stopped him from attending the tournament in North America. However, on the evidence of his composed performance against North Macedonia, he’s got every reason to believe he won’t need to watch from afar when Scotland next travel to a major tournament.

“I didn’t go [to the World Cup] - it was too expensive for me!” laughed Graham. “I was just like everyone else, watching in the pub with their mates. It was pretty amazing and hopefully I can be part of something like that one day. I wasn’t too far away, Steve Clarke told me. It’s just about trusting myself now and hopefully get there one day.”

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

On seven minutes Sheaf put the ball inside to Henry McDonald and he hit a shot on the turn and low. Billy Collings did well though to divert it wide.

Ethan Robb latched on to a ball in midfield and picked out Roberts on the left but after speeding down the wing his cross flew over the bar. In 17 minutes Cal Laycock found Roberts and he sped on before shooting wide from the edge of the box.

Golds’ Harry Heath was a nuisance and forced a save from Tommy Scott at his near post. Then Matthew Storm lost possession to Laycock who ran through into the box but his strike was easily saved on 27 minutes.

Benny Read – a new Rocks signing from Gosport – made a mistake as Dion Jarvis stole the ball before picking out Gaskin but with only Scott to beat, he hit it straight at the keeper.

Jarvis and Robb were booked after a tackle by Bognor's defensive midfielder. Heath also went into the book and Sheaf had to come off with what looked like a hamstring injury. Harvey Whyte replaced him on 37 minutes.

Bognor went close in the second minute of first half stoppage time. Henry Nevill worked himself the box but his shot crashed off the post.

It didn't take long for Bognor to take the lead in the second half. Read put a pass inside to Laycock and he had beaten the offside trap and turned and coolly slotted the ball into the bottom corner on 47 minutes.

Scott Faber lashed out with a challenge on Robb and went into the book on 57 minutes.

Bognor extended their lead in the 59th minute as Josh Batt lashed a loose ball into the net on the half-volley after a long free-kick by Kaya Tshaka.

On 64 minutes Bognor made a double change as Laycock and McDonald made way for Oliver Lovell and Charlie Gunson.

The Golds got a goal back directly from a corner as Gaskin headed in from a 69th minute delivery. Then Gaskin put in a dangerous ball across from the left but Lewis Olajide flashed it wide.

Jarvis blasted over as Littlehampton swung the momentum to their advantage.

Ben Anderson and Louie Williams replaced Robb and Read for Bognor in the 76th minute.

Tshaka was battling in midfeld and was unlucky to lose possession. A long ball saw Heath run powerfully into the area but Scott was quick out of his goal to bravely stop him.

Williams was booked for simulation on 87 minutes as he seemed to lost his footing in the box.

It was a real battle in the closing moments as Williams was holding up the ball for Bognor where he could. But Littlehampton posed a threat with some quick play and long throws from the dangerous Heath.

Five minutes were added but Bognor held on to move third in the division.

Booed off the park by sections of the home crowd at the break, McGinn admits he takes no issue with the Tartan Army voicing their displeasure at the team’s on-pitch displays, but has pleaded with them to vent their ire at himself and the more experienced names in Scotland’s dressing room than the fresh faces as they look to adjust to Pocognoli’s methods.

Get our daily football newsletter by clicking here.

“The manager's got a great reputation and a good record at both places he's went,” said McGinn following his two goal haul. “The most important thing now in football is individuals don't win you games. It's unity, teamwork and everyone on the same page. And you see how successful clubs do it, successful countries and we want to be one of them. It's not going to happen overnight.

“There's a lot to learn but we did create big chances in the game where we could have scored three, four or five and it could be a different story. This isn't something that gets fixed in March or even next September. it will start to build over the next 18 months. I think the young players are starting to show now more. Luke Graham tonight, I thought he was brilliant, it's not easy playing in the middle of a back three.

“He's been waiting for his chance and the manager's shown that if you deserve your chance you're going to get put in there. So we need players like Luke, Porto [Ryan Porteous] coming back, Doaky [Ben Gannon-Doak] showed glimpses tonight. So we've got so many players that can step up and they will. We just need to show that belief and take it to pitch.”

Asked if he felt the fans need to show patience, McGinn said: “Maybe a bit. I understand it's frustrating; it's freezing, you want to see four, five, six goals, but the balance has got to be there. They're entitled to their opinion, but there's got to be a mixture of patience. But at the same time, the supporters are entitled to say whatever they like. But just as long as they hurl anything they want to shout at the experienced boys. Just let the young ones flourish and try to settle into the team.”

Awarded player of the match against North Macedonia, the 31-year-old’s brace shot himself into joint-third in Scotland’s record goalscorers list. McGinn’s international goal tally is now 24, drawing level with Hughie Gallacher, six short of Kenny Dalglish and Denis Law. Asked if it had sunk in yet, the former Hibs man kept his focus on the team, insisting Monday’s clash against Switzerland holds more importance as they look to give themselves a chance of qualifying for the Nations League playoffs.

“A bit strange obviously but at the minute that's gone to the back burner,” said McGinn. “We need to play slightly better. We know that but we're going through a period which I've been used to at club level, a lot of changes, a lot of detail that we need to try and remember and get used to. It's about sticking at it. We're keen to play a style of football that's not easy but it's going to get bums off seats.

“It takes time, over a few years now at club level it's been the exact same for us but the supporters stuck with us, the players stuck at it and it's important that everyone believes in it because if one person drops off or doesn't believe in it that's when it all starts to fall apart. We've got an important win but there's definitely a lot of room for improvement.

“It’s difficult, I know they [Switzerland] drew [vs Slovenia] but they've got a couple of players back that they were missing last time. We want to be competing against these teams away from home, playing the same way. We're going to stick at it, it's not going to be perfect for a while but on Monday night we're no different.”

#1876. Ibrahimovic shares feelings on ‘bond’ with Milan: “The most important team in my life”

Zlatan Ibrahimovic has shed light on just how much AC Milan mean to him, labelling it the ‘most important’ club he has represented.

Today marks the launch of ‘Il Milan nel Mondo’, Mauro Suma’s new book exploring the Rossoneri’s reach beyond both Milan and Italy. Several Rossoneri Legends will join the author at the launch this morning, including Daniele Massaro, Demetrio Albertini and Filippo Galli.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Ibrahimovic wrote a foreword in the book, which has been relayed by MilanNews. The RedBird Capital senior advisor spoke about just how much the club means to him, after his two spells as a player and now his time as an executive.

“Milan are the most important team in my life. And it’s also the only one that convinced me to return. In my career, I’ve worn legendary shirts, played in wonderful cities, and won everywhere. But Milan was something different,” he said.

“It was the only club that truly drew me back, the only one where I felt the need to start over. Convincing Zlatan to return isn’t easy. It’s not easy for anyone. Yet, with Milan, it’s happened more than once.

“This means that between me and these colours, a bond has been created that goes beyond football, beyond trophies, even beyond time. Victory remains in the halls of fame; some teams, however, stay with you. AC Milan belongs to this category.

“The first time, AC Milan brought me happiness, the second, love. In the Rossoneri, I found a sense of belonging that is increasingly rare in modern football. Because starting an adventure with a club can happen. Returning a second time, and then again, means that the club and its fans have become part of you.

“AC Milan are the most successful Italian club at international level, but it’s not just a collection of trophies. It’s an identity. It’s a way of being in football and in the world. Wherever it goes, it leaves a mark. And those who join AC Milan, sometimes, never leave.”

Ibrahimovic signed the first time in August 2010 after an experience at Barcelona that wasn’t a positive one, and he helped Milan to the Scudetto with a 14-goal haul. He won the Capocannoniere the next season, doubling that tally.

He returned in 2019 and scored 25 goals in 37 appearances in his first two campaigns, securing a return to European competitions. At the end of his third season, the climb was complete: the Rossoneri won their 19th league title.

Then, in June 2023 came his emotional farewell at San Siro, before Zlatan returned to the club but wearing a suit and tie.

#1873. Sebastien Pocognoli believes Scotland ‘click’ is coming for player who served up a curate’s egg at Hampden

After 12 games so far, from Liverpool to Ljubljana, from Miami to North Macedonia, the ‘No Scotland, no party’ world tour of 2026 grinds into St Gallen on Monday for one final performance.

What a 12 months it’s been. Scotland at least managed to avoid going a whole calendar year without winning a competitive game at Hampden by narrowly overcoming North Macedonia in the Nations League on Friday night.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

It’s a small triumph considering Scotland were hoping to make history a few months ago by qualifying for the second stage of a major tournament for the first time. So this is where we are, which is where exactly? Wrestling with a system that looks increasingly unsuited to Scotland. Rather than freeing them up, which was Sebastien Pocognoli’s manifesto when he took over, his preferred 3-4-1-2 formation seems to have put the players in a straitjacket. The idea was to play ten yards further forward. Instead, Scotland appear to be going backwards in every sense.

They nevertheless have the chance to end the international year with a truly eye-popping result if they can beat Switzerland, already confirmed as Group B1 winners. It is the 13th match in a year where Scotland have played teams from five of the six FIFA confederations. Six of the matches, including Monday, have been against teams in the top 20 of the Fifa rankings. This perhaps explains the unexceptional total of just five wins, two of them friendlies.

Scotland need another victory on Monday and must hope Slovenia don’t take three points their trip to North Macedonia to finish in the top two and earn a promotion chance via the play-offs this Spring. It’s been a challenging as well as often very memorable year.

The danger is Scotland are already all played out, no one more so than Andy Robertson. No one except Kenny Dalglish has appeared as many times for Scotland as the skipper. Robertson has survived the risk of suspension and will become Scotland’s most capped ever player when, fitness permitting, he lines up on Monday.

Ryan Christie came on for his 75th cap on Friday, while Kieran Tierney, if selected, will earn cap No. 60 against Switzerland. Scott McTominay, meanwhile, will hit the 75-mark.

No one’s getting any younger. But Pocognoli seems determined to keep faith with a system that demands dynamism.

“I think we need to rest well,” he said. “That is the first thing. If we want to play like this we need energy. I will need to consider the best approach for the game regarding the quality and also the fitness of some players. We have some players in the squad who we have to manage. They cannot play two games in a row.”

Aaron Hickey might be one of those, hence him being named among the substitutes for the supposedly less testing fixture against North Macedonia. If he comes back into the side against Switzerland what does that mean for Ben Gannon-Doak? The winger featured at right wing-back and once again produced a curate’s egg of a performance. Good in parts, including when he won Scotland’s match-winning penalty (although even that was after he had taken a poor touch).

The focus and indeed expectation placed on him seems completely unreasonable, although he possibly hasn’t helped himself. It’s what happens when you are named man of the match for Bournemouth in a 3-0 Europa League win over AC Milan.

But this does not mean there's been an overnight cure for the imperfections that dog the player, understandably so given he’s only just turned 21. Pocognoli believes things will “click” for him in time. The right choice will suddenly become his instinctive reaction. The final ball will become a weapon rather than his Achilles heel. “We know that he needs to improve on the end product,” said Pocognoli. “But he created a penalty and against Slovenia and North Macedonia away he created a number of unbelievable one v ones. He did that (on Friday) as well.

“I believe in one moment he will have a click about decision making. I believe if he is playing every game he can make (better) decisions….. he knows that he only has to play a game every two weeks sometimes he can (over)think, ‘This is my moment.’ It is a process. He will become older and will at some point become relaxed in his decision making.”

Whether Gannon-Doak ever achieves his potential might hinge on playing where he ought to be playing, which is as an out-and-out winger. At present, Pocognoli’s preferred formation won’t accommodate this. It’s unlikely that the Belgian is going to change his ways ahead of Monday, when Scotland might really need three centre halves (even if one of them is really a full back).

Former Dundee defender Luke Graham’s assured performance aged just 22 surely means he will line up once more in the middle of defence.

“I have really scanned the quality of the squad and I believe we have the quality to play like this,” said Pocognoli. “I believe that Luke Graham can be important to the defence. “I believe Kieran Tierney can be good in that position. I believe that Ryan Porteous is helpful for how we want to play because he is on the front foot."

Pocognoli mentioned his adherence to a midfield 'box', where Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson act as pivots. “We need speed if we want to use the box,” he said. “We have that with Ben, but we don’t have that unlimited specific quality.

“It is up to me to find the best way to play,” he added. “But it is not easy to bring players who come from different clubs with a different approach to fit into (the system) in two days. But we have a lot of players who play that way in Italy and other places. It has helped me a lot in the past.”

The past is history. Never mind Gannon-Doak, things need to start clicking sooner rather than later for Pocognoli.

#1871. It’s agony for Worthing at Scunthorpe as 93rd minute goal denies them another away win

Jordan Young gave the away side a half-time advantage with a well-taken effort on 17 minutes, but the Rebels backline could not quitewithstand the Iron’s second half resurgence and Eastbourne-raised Norwood came up with the late leveller for new boss Andy Preece.

It was gutting for Adam Hinshelwood and his players and the manager was shown a red card at full-time. But the Rebels remain in the play-off one, in seventh place.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Returning after an 11-day break from action, the side featured two changes to the eleven that began the 3-0 defeat by Sutton United in their last league outing.

Harrison Foulkes regained his place in goal while Charlie Waller returned to the defensive unit. New signing Sam Clucas featured on the bench, with Daniel Isichei also named amongst the substitutes.

A sense of optimism among the home faithful in Preece’s first game at the helm was combatted by a strong start from the away side, spearheaded by the dynamic movement of Young to initiate some promising moves early on.

Having asserted themselves on the ball through the opening quarter of an hour, the Rebels found the breakthrough in the 17th minute. Brilliant link-up between Kendall and Young saw the latter pick up the ball in a central position just outside the box. The former Torquay United man let off a fierce low effort on his left side which clipped off the foot of Maison Campbell’s left post before nestling inside the opposite upright.

The movement of Razzaq Coleman De-Graft and Young to pick up space behind the Iron midfield gave the away side a constant outlet on the break, from which they were able to fashion several dangerous breakaways.

Scunthorpe came close to drawing level with three minutes of normal time remaining at the end of the first half. An in-swinging corner delivery was swept onto the crossbar by Kyle Hurst, before Norwood saw two follow-up attempts blocked from just outside the six-yard box.

The Rebels’ counter-attacking prowess remained their best route towards goal heading into the break, with Kendall having a good chance to double the visitors’ lead 90 seconds before the interval.

After jinking away from one challenge at the edge of the box, the forward drilled a low effort narrowly wide of the mark down to Campbell’s left-hand side.

Having grown into the game towards the end of the first 45 minutes, Preece’s hosts started the second half with renewed intensity, keeping play largely in the Worthing half as Adam Hinshelwood’s side were forced to defend their box.

Alfie Beestin had two attempts on goal, first being denied by Foulkes from a long throw before having a strike blocked from around 20 yards.

The attacking movement and nuisance of Norwood lent itself to Scunthorpe’s direct approach to getting back level, with the former Oldham striker constantly winning first balls.

Just after the hour mark, Pat Jones’ delivery from the right flank was stabbed over the bar by Norwood at the edge of the six-yard box, as tight defending from Joe Cook and Jayden Moore prevented the veteran from getting a more telling touch.

Pressure continued to mount on Worthing with minutes ticking away. With two minutes of the 90 to play, the Attis Arena was plunged into momentary silence as substitute Declan Howe’s header deflected agonisingly wide.

With 30 seconds remaining of three additional minutes, all the resolute defending from the visitors came undone as Scunthorpe found a leveller. After the away side surrendered possession inside their own half, Howe’s clipped ball towards the back post was headed back across goal and eventually poked home by Norwood.

It was a gutting conclusion from a Rebels perspective, especially for Foulkes, who commanded his box astutely through numerous waves of lofted deliveries into the area.

#1868. Who is Mario Frick? The new manager at Aberdeen who scored at Hampden, lost to Hibs and develops players

Mario Frick says he will create an environment at Aberdeen “where his players can thrive” after being appointed the next manager of the Pittodrie outfit.

Former Luzern boss Frick takes over from Stephen Robinson, who was sacked on Monday by Aberdeen with the team languishing in 11th place in the Premiership. The length of his contract has not been disclosed.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Dons hierarchy have moved quickly to land his successor and after a week of interviews have settled on former Liechtenstein striker Frick, 52, who has been out of work since the summer after end a five-year spell in Switzerland with Luzern.

Frick has also managed FC Balzers and FC Vaduz in his homeland. He will be assisted by Roman Matter, a 44-year-old Swiss coach who was also at Luzern. The pair are due to arrive in Aberdeen imminently ahead of Saturday’s league match against bottom club Kilmarnock.

“I'm excited to be joining Aberdeen FC,” said Frick. “It's a club with a proud history, passionate supporters and big ambitions.

“Together with the staff, my aim is to create an environment where the players can thrive, develop and perform at their very best, while working towards our goals as a team.”

Chief executive Adrian Bevington revealed Frick was the “unanimous” choice of the Aberdeen board after going through a robust process to identify him.

“We are delighted to welcome Mario Frick and his assistant coach Roman Matter to Aberdeen Football Club,” said Bevington. “This appointment follows a thorough and extensive recruitment process led by [sporting director] Lutz Pfannenstiel and myself on behalf of the board, during which we spoke to a number of highly qualified candidates.

“Mario has significant experience as a head coach and has delivered impressive results with both Vaduz and Luzern. He has a proven track record of building competitive teams and developing young players.

“Throughout our discussions, he demonstrated a clear vision, strong leadership qualities and a deep understanding of what is required to build a successful team.

“He was also exceptionally well regarded by the many people across the game we consulted during the process, and the Board was unanimous in its belief that he is the right person to lead Aberdeen Football Club forward.

“I would like to thank the board, in particular Willie Garner, and colleagues across the club for their diligence and support throughout this process.”

Pfannenstiel tipped Frick to have a “real impact at Pittodrie” and said his character will be crucial as the Dons look to climb the league table.

“I’m really pleased that we have been able to bring Mario Frick to Aberdeen,” said Pfannenstiel. “I have enormous respect for his football knowledge, leadership qualities and passion for the game.

“Mario is a strong personality with clear ideas about how he wants his teams to play. He brings energy, ambition and a winning mentality, and knows how to build a strong team environment.

“We were looking for the right person to lead the next chapter of Aberdeen FC, and I’m convinced Mario has the qualities, character and vision to make a real impact. I’m looking forward to working closely with him.”

Born in the Swiss town of Chur, Frick carved out a playing career as a physical striker and holds the record number of caps for Liechtenstein, scoring 16 goals in 125 appearances. One of those strikes came at Hampden in a 2-1 defeat by Scotland in 2010.

Also deployed as a centre-half, Frick played for clubs such as FC Basel, FC Zürich, St. Gallen, Grasshopper, Siena and Ternana before hanging up his boots in 2016 and moving into coaching.

At Vaduz, he secured promotion to the Swiss Super League, which earned him a move to Luzern. He spent five years with them, landing a fourth-placed finish. He faced Hibs in the 2024 Conference League, losing 5-3 on aggregate.

Frick most used formation with Vaduz and Luzern was a 4-4-2 diamond and he has carved out a reputation as a head coach who has developed younger players, most notably AC Milan and Switzerland midfielder Ardon Jashari.

#1867. Sharpe by name, sharp by nature: Antoine lifts Lancing to big win over Pagham

Manager Dale Hurley was proud of the Lancers performance, which he described as very efficient.The clean sheet particularly pleased him and it was no understatement for him to point out that, with a bit of luck, the goal tally could have been even higher.

The result demonstrated the progress Lancing have made since a shaky beginning to the season and they now occupy 14th place.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Lancing had a dream start, taking the lead with five minutes gone. Gabe Robinson used his pace to break clear down the right, hitting a fine low cross for Antoine Sharpe to run on to and strike against the upright. Sharpe by name, sharp by nature – he was quickest to react to the loose ball and squeeze it at across the line.

Mo Khedidji and Robinson were a constant threat to the Lions left, using their pace and close control. A tricky run by Khedidji saw him switch the ball to Robinson, who laid the ball across to Rob Deda, whose effort was narrowly high.

Deda then turned provider, winning the ball before a slide-rule pass put Khedidji into the box to finish coolly.

Sharpe was denied a clear run on goal when the referee decided to award Lancing a free-kick for a foul on Robinson, rather than allow adavantage.

The Lions were working hard to reduce the arrears .Alfie Davidson wriggled clear of Khedidji and floated in a cross that was met with a volley which cleared the bar. The Lions’ first shot on target came from Toby Hewitt but Elliot Dailly dealt with it.

The goal of the game came on 38 minutes .The ball reached Sharpe just outside the box. He allowed it to drop before volleying it out of reach of keeper Kelly and into the top corner.

The three-goal lead came close to being reduced shortly before half-time but Elliot Dailly pulled off an excellent save to preserve the three-goal margin.

Lancing inroduced Kaiden Hummerston at the restart for Deda. Lancing began where they left off with Robinson, Sharpe and Khedidji too hot for the Lions to handle and it took barely three minutes for Sharpe to sprint clear through the middle, with only the keeper to beat. A well-placed strike into the bottom corner gave the attacker his hat-trick.

Pagham threatened with a dangerous cross from the right which flew across the Lancing six-yard box but it eluded everyone.

Sharpe came close to a fourth when picked out by a sublime pass from Khedidji.He fired the ball with real venom but it rattled the underside of the bar before being cleared. This was his last meaningful action as he was given a well deserved break with Dylan Hurst coming on.

Some clever interplay between Billy McKay, Robinson and Khedidji culminated in a deep cross which proved just too high for Alek Amissah, on for Kai Birchley, to get his head to.

Robinson broke clear down the left, cut in on his right and forced a good save from Kelly.

With 71 minutes gone Lancing were in dreamland when Oliver Deda got his head to the ball at a corner to put his side five up.

Khedidji ,set up by fine pass from Ryan Plummer, executed a delicate chip which was well saved by keeper Kelly. McKay ,a real dynamo in Lancing’s midfield, made way for Dylan Walter.

The Lions were striving to salvage at least a consolation but were denied by another excellent save by Dailly and Lancing finished the stronger with a good strike from Archie McGonigle which Kelly held. In the closing minutes, a strong run from deep by Ryan Gummer saw him come close with a shot which grazed the bar.

#1866. Ex-Premier League ref calls Mikel Arteta a ‘nightmare’ to deal with

Former Premier League referee Graham Scott has named Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta as the toughest person to deal with on the touchline.

Last month, Arteta received his second yellow card of the season during Arsenal’s 2-0 win over Everton but said after the game that he had a dossier of other managers committing similar offences which have gone unpunished.

The Arsenal manager now faces a one-match touchline ban if he receives a third yellow card.

Scott, who refereed in the Premier League for a decade before retiring in 2025, claims Arteta ‘does push all the limits all of the time’ and described the Spaniard as ‘hard work’.

When asked who was the worst manager to deal with on the touchline, Scott told The Athletic: ‘Well, the trite answer is all of them when they’re losing.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The honest answer, I’m afraid, I know whatever I say at this point just gets me pelters but it is Arteta. He is the hardest work.

‘He really does push all the limits all of the time. I don’t mind that in many ways, he’s trying to get a competitive advantage for his team. That’s fine. That’s part of his job. And of course, he’s entitled to do it, and it’s for us to place them, but he does make your life extremely difficult.

‘He’s out of his box [technical area] all the time. I watched him recently in the game against Everton and every time Everton had the ball anywhere near the touchline on his side, he was like joining in the press, his toes are on the touchline.

‘As fourth official, it’s a nightmare, because if you step forward and do anything about it, you’re being pedantic, being petty. He does get away with rather too much. The officials do need to be a bit tighter. And I was one of them who let him do that. I’m not going to deny that. But he was just hard work. Really, really hard work all the time in a way that others tended to be hard work some of the time.

‘And let’s not pretend the others are all, by comparison, angelic. Some were very controlled. Graham Potter would be an example. Didn’t have anything to do with you, just very, very calm, quiet. Both shown respective costly bookings against Denmark on Sunday night, the duo of Ruben Dias and Benfica midfielder Joao Palhinha will miss out through suspension here. Registering four direct goal contributions in his five Nations League appearances this year (three goals, one assist), AC Milan striker Goncalo Ramos will spearhead Portugal’s attack.

Blown away in Braga on Sunday as they slumped to that shock 4-1 drumming against Denmark, Portugal will be searching for an immediate Nations League response here. Nevertheless, already cruising their way to a knockout stage ticket, Jesus’ superstar squad have their sights set on defending their Nations League crown. Opening proceedings with a 1-0 victory against the Dragons back on September 24th, Portugal will be looking to exploit a Wales squad who have already accepted they will finish rock-bottom of the League A standings.

#1860. Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono handed ban for tackle that led to Jesus de Miguel death

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games for his tackle that resulted in the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

The 25-year-old was sent off after his collision with De Miguel near the halfway line late in the Spanish second division match on November 2.

De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest after Owono’s knee had struck him in the chest. The 30-year-old striker was taken to hospital where he died the following morning.

The Spanish Football Federation’s disciplinary committee has now issued the maximum suspension possible for Owono’s challenge.

A statement said: ‘The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play’.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesus de Miguel, is public knowledge. In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances… the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.’

In his first statement since De Miguel’s death, Owono insisted he will ‘face whatever comes with the utmost respect’.

‘These are the most difficult days of my life. I’m struggling to find the words and finding it very hard to process what has happened,’ Owono said.

‘I feel immense pain at the loss of Jesus. I’m thinking of him, his family, and all the people who loved him.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I can’t think of anything other than Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.’

Speaking this week, FC Andorra manager Carles Manso said that Owono is still considering his future in football.

‘He is deeply affected by the situation,’ Manso said.

‘We will give him the space to feel completely free to decide whether, and when, he might want to return.’

Earlier this week, Spanish newspaper Marca reported that Owono is barely leaving his house following De Miguel’s death and is closely working with psychologists and doctors.

#1859. Wigan Athletic 2 Barnsley 1: Keeping the faith is tough as Reds hit new low

Barnsley were the ones left dishevelled and on the floor by the end.

A single-digit points haul by the second half of November, their season is currently in pieces. Fifty points seems a long way off.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

These lot will give you a chance is the sentence that every opposing League One manager must surely utter when talk turns to Barnsley.

A well-meaning, nice group of boys who say - and hope to do - the right things, Barnsley don’t last the course, unfortunately.

You don't have to play particularly well to beat them and that is a considerable worry.

They have been in most games this season, but eventually err.

Concentration, physicality and sensing danger are all areas where this group are deficient. A disturbing cocktail. They don’t handle pressure, quite simply and their game management is lamentable.

Barnsley have lost their last five away league matches. Their concession of 17 goals in the second half of games is the joint-worst record in the third tier.

The 23rd-placed Reds, only kept off the bottom by goal difference, are winless in nine league matches since September 2. Autumn, certainly on the league front, has been appalling.

Ahead of kick-off, the Monkees "I’m a Believer" got an airing on the Wigan jukebox. Bob Marley’s classic “Three Little Birds” - a song beloved of Barnsley - did the rounds at the final whistle as Wigan escaped the relegation zone after showing the savvy.

Barnsley should be worried about a number of things, for sure.

As is their manager. Keep the Faith is the motto of the Northern Soul movement - another thing associated with Wigan.

Daniel Stendel was clearly struggling on that count in the immediate aftermath of events on Saturday.

He spoke about holding discussions with Reds majority shareholder/chairman Neerav Parekh. Not necessarily about his own position - not yet, anyway - but endeavouring to find ways to support a playing squad who plainly need help.

It was all a bit unclear. It wasn't to do with bringing in more free agents either.

Then what was it? Discussing what Barnsley need to do in the January transfer window should be top of the agenda. Even if it feels some way in the distance.

Make no mistake, if the Oakwell outfit get the winter window wrong, then there is a pretty high chance that they will be playing fourth-tier football next season for the first time since 1978-79 unfortunately.

‘Probably as good a place as we’ve been’, was Gary Caldwell’s pre-match take on Wigan’s mood ahead of this one.

In fairness, his Barnsley counterpart - in his second spell at the club much like the Scot - could have said the same on the back of two healthy cup wins. The league is a different matter, alas.

It was the former whose side would build momentum.

A relatively even first half had one key moment.

Fraser Murray had delivered a warning with his sweet curler producing a full-stretch parry from Ceiran Slicker.

A few minutes later, the Reds custodian had no chance when Murray again showed delicious technique to bend an unstoppable low shot into the far corner, for his first goal of the campaign. An important one.

How the ball arrived at his feet, with Wigan afforded an ocean of space in the middle of the pitch was poor from a Reds perspective. Latics also fancied it out wide against both Ziyad Larkeche and Jubril Okedina.

On the resumption, Barnsley found a much-needed lifeline in front of their admirable band of stoic supporters. Luca Connell found Reyes Cleary - who worried Wigan for most of the afternoon.

He expertly manufactured space before fizzing over a superb low cross which was buried by Cam McGeehan, backing up in the box.

It was classic wing-play from Cleary to present an opportunity on a plate for McGeehan, who struck his ninth goal of the campaign.

Barnsley had their tails up, but - all the while - there was a nagging feeling about what might happen at the other end. The fears were borne out in appalling fashion.

Morgan Fox hung up a cross which was attacked by Jensen Weir. Larkeche, having a poor game, challenged meekly and Weir couldn’t believe his luck.

His header caught Slicker by surprise at the near post as he could only pat the effort into the net, horribly. And that was that. A scruffy concession in a bedraggled season. Sheffield Wednesday next.

Wigan Athletic: Whitworth; Burns, Carragher, Fox; Barrett (Trevitt 68), Weir, Power, Mellish; Burrowes (Miller 87), Murray; Saydee (Hogan 67). Substitutes unused: J Walsh, Chilokoa-Mullen, A Harris, Higgins.

#1858. Troy Deeney tells Mauricio Pochettino to axe Man Utd star: ‘Cut them out’

Troy Deeney believes incoming Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino should ‘make a statement’ by looking to sell Marcus Rashford.

Rashford failed to make an impact under Michael Carrick after returning to Old Trafford following his loan spell at Barcelona last season.

The 29-year-old missed the last five matches of Carrick’s tenure due to a hip injury, with Pochettino arriving as his replacement after agreeing a two-and-a-half-year contract with the Red Devils.

Reports earlier this week have suggested that Rashford could be a big winner of United’s latest appointment, with Pochettino very keen to work with the England international and get him back to his best.

But former Premier League striker Deeney believes Pochettino should not be so lenient with Rashford and must be willing to sell the forward in January if he doesn’t get back to his best quickly.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘Poch must go in and take a huge sledgehammer to the toxic Carrington culture, accepting that things are not good enough,’ Deeney told The Sun.

‘Managers and those above need to stop fiddling around the edges and tackle the big problem, otherwise there will be no progress.

‘United supporters might not like it, but Arsenal have shown the way and offered the blueprint. Rather than repeating what has failed, they must make a brave change. Someone big has to go, even if it means short-term pain.

‘Mesut Ozil, Pierre-Emerick Aubameyang and Alexandre Lacazette were pushed out for the benefit of everyone. They were good players but carried a stink with them around the place.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Cut them out and everyone else can breathe, focus in training and start growing.’

Deeney continued: ‘For the Red Devils, that has to be someone like skipper Bruno Fernandes or, once again, Marcus Rashford.

‘I can guarantee it now, Rashford will suddenly be fit for the Liverpool game. He will see a new manager who likes energy and pace, he will think he can do all that.

‘He might even start well, get a few games, but then Pochettino will ask for more and he will not like it. Then all the bad traits will come back — he’ll be out and about and late for training all over again. The cycle begins and the damage returns.

‘Pochettino must make a statement, give these players until January to prove they are on board or get rid.’

#1857. Di'Shon Bernard goal points to Sheffield Wednesday tweak that can up entertainment levels

Despite the 3-0 scoreline over Plymouth Argyle, Challinor's first league game as Owls manager only really delivered on the first front.

But it would be unreasonable to expect an instant transformation, especially with injuries forcing players into unfamiliar positions.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

After six games without a win and cup defeats in Challinor's first two matches, Wednesday just needed to get over the line.

But on an afternoon where the football never rivalled Plymouth's orange away kit for brightness, one moment really stood out.

It was born of a mistake, Di'Shon Bernard failing to find Keillor-Dunn after winning the ball deep in Wednesday territory.

But when Malachi Boateng's interception turned into a one-two and the centre-back drove into shooting range and scored in off a post.

The game already won by Keillor-Dunn's finish two minutes earlier, it was no more than the cherry on the cake, six games into Bernard’s return from a 19-month knee injury.

But the story of Henrik Pedersen's tenure was clear – excited by the potential of David Storch’s ownership, Owls fans are greedy. They do not just want the cake, they want the cherries too. After the thin gruel of last season, who can blame them?

"I want people to be brave," said Challinor. "If the shot goes into the Kop, so be it. I'll always encourage people to make positive decisions.

"They're going to make mistakes. We're going to ask them to do things that are different.

"Of course we'll get frustrated, but that's acceptable. That's on us and that will always be the case."

Wednesday's shape flitted between a 4-2-3-1 and a 3-2-4-1 when Sil Swinkels tucked from left-back into a more familiar position.

Back threes need a player willing to break out, especially on days – not Saturday, in fairness – when the visitors come to S6 to frustrate.

"We should, if we do things right, come up against more blocks and teams getting men behind the ball,” argued Challinor.

"That's when people need to step in, be positive and make the most of opportunities. That comes from backing yourself, and quality."

Bernard, a team-mate of Marcus Rashford in the Manchester United youth ranks, has that.

"He wants to put his body on the line," commented Challinor. "He got injured at Notts County by blocking a shot and opening his knee up.

"There's loads of work we can do with him, he can get so much better.

"We'll ask him to be better and more positive in possession as well as being able to do the other things."

When pressed into giving the ball up in the 37th minute he got back to kill the move when it came into the penalty area. When Xavier Amaechi threatened to force his way through, Bernard refused to be shaken off and made an excellent recovery tackle.

He believes working with Challinor and his assistant Clint Hill – more no-nonsense centre-backs in their day – can elevate his game.

"Playing the right of a three he's trusting me to do more on the ball," he says. "Before I got injured, that was probably one of my strengths.

"Now I need to really just build up the confidence to do more of it because you can see in glimpses I am capable of it.

"He's pushing me to be that player and I'm grateful him and his staff have shown that's what I need to do."

For the 80 minutes before those two goals in two minutes there was not a great deal to write home about.

The fizzing atmosphere Challinor was looking forward to after only tasting Hillsborough-lite in the EFL Trophy was flat for an hour because Wednesday's football was.

Although they were fortunate Roman Curtis' chest high tackle on Jamal Lowe only got a yellow card, Plymouth should have gone in at half-time multiple goals up.

Instead, when Bernard's goalbound header was nodded over at the end of the first half, Billy Mitchell’s deflected shot from the corner brought his first goal since 2021.

The second half was more even but Hillsborough helped its team over the line.

Having missed an easy chance from a quick throw-in, Keillor-Dunn poked home the loose ball at a badly-defended free-kick and at 2-0 the contest was over.

But the mouth-watering bit was still to come.

Sheffield Wednesday: Lumley; Valery, Bernard, Cooper, Swinkels; Mitchell, Heskey; Slattery, Bannan (Barry 72), J Lowe (Palmer 85); Keillor-Dunn (Gray 85).

Unused substitutes: Santos, Trueman, Weaver, Thornton.

Plymouth Argyle: Cooper; Harding, MacKenzie (Irow 63), Hartridge; Curtis, Boateng, White (Oseni 77), Ross; Amaechi, Ibrahim (Watts 63); Evans.

Unused substitutes: Storer, Campbell, Mwaro, Maund.

​The misses: Plymouth spurned some great chances, Xavier Amaechi horribly failing to make contact with a ball in from Bradley Ibrahim, then heading a great second-half chance from a Alex Hartridge cross wide. Earlier, Will Evans cushioned a volley into the side netting when Joe Lumley’s flapping at a corner left the goal gaping.

Star performers: Di’Shon Bernard was excellent but so too was midfielder Billy Mitchell, the stand-out Owls player in a first half where they were well below par.

Run over: This was the first time in eight league games Hillsborough’s attendance had officially fallen below 30,000 – though only by 772. The football did not lift them in the first half but they took it upon themselves to inspire the players around the hour.

#1855. How Harrogate Town banished ghosts of Carlisle United with 4-0 rout of Altrincham - analysis

When Altrincham defender Reuben Lopata-White lunged in on Harrogate Town winger Ellis Taylor, there will have been two shivers down the spines of the home supporters.

The first one being the natural one, brought on by the reckless nature of the loaned-out Leeds United prospect’s foul. The second will have been prompted by the dawning realisation of what comes next.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Harrogate have not had the best of times against 10-man sides and lost 3-0 to a Carlisle United side who saw two men sent off less than three weeks ago.

Halloween has been and gone, but the ghosts of Carlisle threatened to haunt when the red card was brandished on the 13-minute mark.

“I think everyone in the stadium thought that [it was going to be a struggle],” said Harrogate boss Simon Weaver. “[Altrincham] probably, ultimately, were buoyed by the fact that it didn't go our way the last time.

“It's not a case of sulking and berating everyone when it just didn't work on that occasion, but are we capable of next time, especially against a really good team like Altrincham, carrying out our roles a bit better?”

To say Harrogate carried out their roles a bit better would be an understatement. The strong Sulphurite grip on the game rarely loosened as they cruised to an emphatic 4-0 win.

It took until the second half but once the hosts started firing on all cylinders in the final third, the afternoon raced away from the Robins.

Will McGowan drew first blood shortly after the restart and Morgan Williams pounced merely 10 minutes later.

Pressure continued to be applied and the advantage was built upon by Michael Craig and Rohan Vaughan, who both hammered home thunderous strikes.

Ellis Taylor may not have etched his name on the scoresheet but the Marcy Fitness Stadium became his playground, one in which he toyed with defenders with relative ease.

“We still had to be very patient,” said Weaver. “[We had] to really break through and put the game to bed.

“We did in the end and that's what mattered and a growing maturity I thought the lads showed today.

“You’ve got to kill off the hope, kill off the energy and psychologically I think the best way of doing it is to keep the ball and keep probing and not get flustered ourselves.”

Boreham Wood have steamed away at the top of the National League table but it remains early days. Harrogate reduced the gap between the sides to 10 points and will be keen to keep chipping away.

As for the ghosts of Carlisle - consider them banished.

“I think we've got a really good, honest group,” said Weaver. “There’s blips on the journey of every team but 18 new players and people are handling disappointments well, people aren't getting over the top or egotistical when we bang a few goals in.

“They want to play and they want to play in the right way but not play boring football. We’ve got a proud record at home.”

#1854. Prediction: Denmark vs Norway

In what is a must-win Nations League showdown on Tuesday night, Denmark will welcome bitter rivals Norway to Copenhagen.

With the League A group campaigns set to be decided in midweek, there are plenty of attractive Nations League betting promotions available.

Ahead of Tuesday’s battle in Copenhagen, you can find all of the key Denmark vs Norway H2H stats here.

Verdict: Antonio Nusa over 0.5 shots on target

Starting with the hosts, producing what was an iconic performance on foreign soil over the weekend as they stormed their way to a 4-1 romp against reigning Nations League champions Portugal, Denmark will be desperately seeking a repeat display here. Sat firmly in the driving seat to punch their respective knockout stage ticket in Copenhagen, Brian Riemer’s side are enjoying an extended flurry. Signing off September’s extended international break with a gritty 1-0 victory against Wales in Cardiff, Denmark have won three of their previous four Nations League appearances. However, getting October underway with a rollercoaster 4-2 defeat against Portugal, Tuesday’s hosts are searching for some essential defensive stability. In fact, Riemer’s men have failed to register consecutive clean sheets across all competitions over the past 13 months.

While Manchester United defender Patrick Drogu might have recently return from a long-term hamstring injury, the 22-year-old has not been included in Denmark’s squad this month. Likewise, despite working his way back to full fitness after sustaining an extended thigh issue, Barcelona’s Andreas Christensen will also not feature here.

Although Fulham star Joachim Andersen might have not made a single Premier League appearance over the past couple of months, the former Crystal Palace defender will keep his spot at the heart of Denmark’s defence. Bagging a sensational Nations League brace against Portugal on Saturday, Napoli striker Rasmus Hojlund will lead the line in Copenhagen.

As for the visitors, making what was an essential return to winning ways over the weekend, Norway have managed to keep their knockout stage dreams alive ahead of Tuesday’s finale in Copenhagen. Eventually clinching a 3-1 victory at home against Wales on Sunday, Stale Solbakken’s side have gained a reputation for their lively outcomes extending on from their World Cup adventure in North America. Signing off September’s extended international break with three consecutive Nations League defeats, Norway are also desperately searching for some kind of defensive steel. Despite opening their League A charge with a rollercoaster 3-2 victory against Tuesday’s hosts on September 24th, Solbakken’s camp have remarkably seen all of their previous 13 straight showdowns across all fronts finish with both teams finding the net.

Once again finding the net against Wales on Saturday evening and notching four goals in his five Nations League appearances this year, Manchester City record-breaker Erling Haaland will lead the line here. Likewise, enjoying what has become a breakout campaign with RB Leipzig this season and also bagging a maiden League A strike in Oslo, the red-hot Antonio Nusa will partner Haaland in attack.

Sustaining a reported ankle injury prior to this month’s international break, Crystal Palace striker Jorgen Larsen has not been included in Norway’s squad. Establishing his spot as Solbakken’s number once choice, Brest shot-stopper Egil Selvik will start between the sticks.

With a Nations League knockout stage ticket still hanging in the balance on Tuesday night, we could be set for a blockbuster battle from Copenhagen. Watching Norway claimed a thrilling 3-2 victory when they met their historic rivals back on September 24th, both camps have gained a reputation for their lively outcomes. Along with Norway remarkably seeing all of their last 13 consecutive appearances finish with both teams finding the net, Denmark have failed to register consecutive clean sheets across all competitions over the past 13 months.

Verdict: Antonio Nusa over 0.5 shots on target

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Former player, manager and pundit Souness has made headlines on more than one occasion in recent months for his controversial comments on England midfield star Rice, saying in the summer on Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored that he might be better suited to playing at centre-back because of his limited passing abilities.

Souness then doubled down on that criticism via the same platform in September, reiterating his belief that Rice might be a central defender and “isn’t the complete midfield player” who perhaps would not get into the team at any of Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich or Manchester City.

He ramped up the rhetoric by saying that Rice was “cheating” in his midfield role with the way he dropped into defence as he called it “old man’s football”.

Rice has now answered those comments when asked in a press conference held ahead of England’s crunch final Nations League group game against Spain in Madrid on Sunday night.

“My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves. For a centre-back, I think that’s not bad numbers!” Rice said with a laugh.

“I think I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals and to be a top-class centre-back getting those numbers I’m delighted with that!

“No, but look, if you speak about, like you said, the positioning, the old man’s football. Look at Harry Kane, for instance.

“We played him the other week [in the Champions League], he dropped next to the centre-backs 20-30 times in the game to pick up the ball. The game’s different now.

“It’s what the game demands, to get away from your man, to get away from who’s marking you, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch.

England hope for triple injury boost amid ‘violent’ All Blacks warning

Winter escapes and activities to end the year in style

“Football’s way different. It’s changed a lot, and you’re always trying to look for tactical advantages.

“In terms of me as a midfielder, I’m constantly watching clips with Mikel [Arteta, Arsenal manager]. He’s constantly coaching me on the pitch.

“How I can progress the ball from deep, how I can drop next to the goalkeeper, how I can go next to full-back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

“So, I feel like we’re now seeing something totally different to what he would see. But in his time football was different, so I totally understand that and, of course, he played in midfield.

“He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There’s no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, as his career, you have to respect what he’s done.

“I didn’t get to see him play but obviously his accolades were top, and I’ve never got to meet him in person.

“If I met him, there wouldn’t be no, like I said, no disrespect. I would speak to him like I would speak to anyone so, yeah, it is what it is.”

Rice also provided an impassioned defence of Arsenal team-mate White, who was once again booed by some England fans after coming off the bench against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday.

It also happened in the friendlies against Uruguay and Japan back in March as the versatile defender made his first appearances for his country since leaving Gareth Southgate’s squad at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

“Ben has moved on from what's happened in the past, he's totally focused on playing for England,” Rice said. “When he's been fit and available he's constantly put himself forward to play for England.

“He loves being here, it's not like he doesn't like being here, he loves playing for England, loves being around the lads.

“If people knew and understood Ben White as a character he's not fazed by anything, he goes with the flow and he just wants to play football and for England.

“Fans are entitled to their opinion, it is what it is but he doesn't feel that way with England. He wants to come out and play his best football and enjoy himself.

“I think that's credit to him, coming on and playing for England and being booed is not easy but the way his character is it really helps him.

“It's not been a conversation for the team. It's so long ago now, it's nearly five years and it doesn't need to keep getting brought up. We need to look forward to the future and what Ben White is going to do in an England shirt, that's the most important thing.

“It's a pointless conversation, Ben has moved on, no one talks about it around the dinner table, no one speaks about it in the pool, we just play football and do what we need to do.”

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Jorge Jesus rubbished suggestions Portugal missed Cristiano Ronaldo as they were humbled 4-1 by Denmark in the Nations League.

All-time great Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football after a public falling out with Portugal head coach Jesus during the September and October Nations League games.

In the first game since Ronaldo's announcement, Portugal put in a woeful display in Braga as Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg's penalty was followed by Rasmus Hojlund's double and a goal for Joachim Andersen.

Bernardo Silva scored a last-gasp consolation for Portugal, who are top of their pool and already through to the quarter-finals.

Plenty of supporters left the stadium early, while many were chanting Ronaldo's name from the stands.

However, Jesus insisted the loss had nothing to do with the absence of 41-year-old Ronaldo.

"One thing has nothing to do with the other. People miss him, they haven't forgotten what Cristiano did for 23 years with the national team," Jesus said.

"There's no going back. Some people left when the team was losing 4-1. Nobody is happy, and we weren't prepared to lose 4-1 today either.

"Missing Cristiano how? If he's no longer in the national team? Only if it's to keep me company. He doesn't play anymore, he's not here, he's already decided his situation."

#1844. Arsenal star sets new goal record after clear transfer message sent

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal striker Viktor Gyokeres set a new Nations League record as his incredible goalscoring run for Sweden continued.

The Gunners forward netted a first-half brace for Graham Potter’s side in Stockholm on Saturday night as they held off a fightback from Bosnia and Herzegovina to win 3-2 in Group B4 and seal promotion back to League A with a game to spare.

Both of Gyokeres’ goals came via penalties, the first he earned himself following a foul by Stjepan Radeljic to put Sweden 2-0 up after only 11 minutes after Daniel Svensson’s early effort.

He slammed in from 12 yards again during first-half stoppage time after Svensson was fouled by ex-Arsenal full-back Sead Kolasinac, who scored himself in the second half after Armin Gigovic’s header to set up a lively finish at Strawberry Arena.

Gyokeres became the first player ever to score in eight consecutive Nations League matches, having notched 12 times during that span - including a memorable four-goal haul against Azerbaijan in November 2024, while he was still at former club Sporting.

He also scored in the away draw with Bosnia and Herzegovina last month, as well as hitting the back of the net home and away against both Romania and Poland, plus in meetings with Slovakia and Estonia.

In total, Gyokeres has 18 goal contributions in his last 11 appearances for Sweden - 14 goals and four assists. His overall record for his country stands at 27 goals in 42 games, good for ninth place on an all-time list led by Zlatan Ibrahimovic that also includes the likes of Henrik Larsson.

He will hope to add further to that tally on Tuesday night, when Potter’s team travel to meet Poland in Wroclaw.

Sweden’s thrilling win over Bosnia and Herzegovina was also notable for the return of Tottenham’s Dejan Kulusevski, who made his first international appearance in almost two years on Saturday following a long-term kneecap injury.

Arsenal will be hoping to benefit from Gyokeres’ strong performances in the Nations League as they seek to maintain or increase their five-point lead at the Premier League summit when they return to action away at struggling Newcastle next weekend.

Only two of his eight goals so far this term have been for his club, in October’s shock Carabao Cup last-16 defeat by fourth-tier Fleetwood and in the 2-1 victory at Slavia Prague in the Champions League earlier this month, when he was excellent.

The 28-year-old - who has received plenty of criticism from fans and pundits for his performances at Arsenal this season - has yet to register at all in the Premier League, where he has made only one start with Kai Havertz remaining manager Mikel Arteta’s preferred option up front.
