#1843. Erling Haaland speaks out on Manchester City future as financial scandal rumbles on

Erling Haaland says he knows little or nothing about the financial scandal Manchester City are involved and is happy at the club, having signed a contract running until 2034.

In September Manchester City were found guilty of over 100 charges relating to breaches of Premier League financial rules.

City were found to have artificially inflated their financial position by over £900 million from 2009-18.

The club is now appealing those guilty verdict, with a hearing taking place in December and a decision on the appeal expected in early 2027.

If the appeal is unsuccessful than punishment is likely to be severe, with points deductions and fines likely and even expulsion from the Premier League a possibility.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

Manchester City’s players have not said much about the situation and continue to compete, although three league defeats on the spin to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest may suggest the situation is taking its toll.

Haaland, though, says he has not even looked into the scandal much, pointing out that he was not at the club during the period of time that has been under investigation.

The 26-year-old scored in Norway’s 3-1 win over Wales on Saturday in Oslo and after successfully converting from the penalty spot, he successfully dodged the issue while speaking to TV2.

‘The investigation covered 2009 to 2018,’ he said. ‘In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2012, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don’t need the whole list…2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne’s first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

‘So this is a question I struggle to answer because it’s a legal battle…It’s a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with.

‘Am I supposed to answer that? I’m not really sure.’

The iconic striker then joked that these questions should be put to his compatriots that were at Manchester City during the time period in question.

Haaland dug out some names that only die hard Manchester City fans wil remember, saying: ‘There were quite a few Norwegians at the club during that period, I think.

‘Abdisalam Ibrahim, Martin Samuelsen and Omar Elabdellaoui were there. Kjetil Haug was there too. I think there were a couple more but I can’t remember.

‘But it’s a difficult question to answer when I don’t really know that much about it. I assume the answers will come… I don’t know when. I haven’t read much about it.

‘To be completely honest, I’m focused on trying to perform for Manchester City. A club I signed a five-year deal with in 2022 and a new nine-and-a-half-year deal in late 2024. I think that says everything.’

Haaland stuck to his guns when asked about his thoughts on his future amid the ongoing appeal process.

‘I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,’ he said. ‘I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

‘I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we’re top of our group in Europe.

‘Things aren’t going so well for City in the league, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can’t focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.’

#1838. Declan Rice fires back at Graeme Souness after criticism from Liverpool legend

Declan Rice has fired back at Graeme Souness after stinging criticism, suggesting the Liverpool legend doesn’t understand how football has changed.

Rice is an integral player for England and Premier League champions Arsenal, widely recognised as one of the best midfielders in the world.

However, Souness has his own view and is not entirely sold on the talents of the 27-year-old, who he believes plays too deep to be considered a complete midfielder.

‘How many times do you see him as the last man with the ball? In the build-up, he’s last man,’ Souness said on Piers Morgan’s Football Uncensored. ‘He’s sitting between two centre-halves or between the centre-half and the full-back. He’s last man. A lot of the time, he doesn’t play in midfield.

‘It’s old man’s football. It’s cheating. An old man’s way of playing midfield. You get the ball under no pressure and you play it out to the full-back.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

He plays too deep to affect the game. I don’t think he’s got enough football. Let me tell you what he can do. He’s the best defensive midfielder in the country right now, he smells danger. But then again, he’s back there all the time.

In 323 Premier League outings for West Ham and Arsenal, Rice has scored 25 goals and provided 35 assists.

He is yet to scored in the top flight during the current campaign, but his five assists are more than any other player in the division.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Responding to the criticism from Souness, Rice said: ‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves. For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’

‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’

Rice pointed out that there are different requirements placed in players in the modern game, using Harry Kane’s pitch-trotting exploits as an example.

‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man’s football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ he said. ‘We played him the other week [Bayern Munich 2-2 Arsenal] and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball.

‘The game is different now. It’s what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It’s changed a lot, and you’re always trying to look for tactical advantages.

Declan Rice hit TWO worldie free-kicks vs Real Madrid 🤯So nice he did it twice ✌️ pic.twitter.com/zg5CzlQQNh

‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I’m constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He’s constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

‘So, I feel like we’re now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There’s no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he’s done.

‘I didn’t get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I’ve never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’

#1837. Erling Haaland issues major transfer update as Man City ‘learn date’ for Premier League appeal decision

Erling Haaland has said he is happy at Manchester City, after commenting on the club’s financial scandal.

During the autumn international break, an independent commission found Man City guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period between 2009/10 and 2018/19.

While City deny any wrongdoing and have launched an appeal, serious sanctions - such as points deductions, fines likely and even expulsion from the Premier League - are likely if that fails.

According to reports, a hearing is to take place in December and a decision on the appeal expected in early 2027.

Should Man City relegated or be issued a huge points deduction, many have speculated that a number of the club’s stars will likely depart, including Haaland.

However, the Norway international - who is valued at £183million on transfermarkt and would have a host of clubs queuing up for his signature were he to leave the Etihad Stadium - has set the record straight on his future with a transfer update.

“I understand that you want a little headline here, but as I said, I signed a long-term contract in 2024,” Haaland told TV2 after scoring in Norway’s 3-1 Nations League win over Wales on Saturday.

“I’d say I made a pretty good choice by joining City in 2022. We can all agree on that.

“I won’t say it myself, but look at the trophies I’ve won and how I’ve developed on and off the pitch. I’m standing here after winning an international 3-1 and we’re top of our group in Europe.

“Things aren’t going so well for City in the league, but we’ll try to turn that around against Fulham. But we can’t focus on that now. Now we have to focus on Denmark.”

Haaland also said that he has not done much research into the investigation as it covers a period when he was not at Man City.

"The investigation covered 2009 to 2018," he added. "In 2009, I played for Bryne U9s. In 2010, the U10s. In 2011, the U11s. 2012, the U12s, 2012, the U13s. Shall we continue? We don’t need the whole list…2014, the U14s. 2015, the U15s and the national team.

"Then the U16s, I think. In 2016, I moved up to Bryne’s first team, second team and youth team. In 2017, I went to Molde. In 2018, I was with Molde. The first team, Molde 2 and a bit with the youth team.

"So this is a question I struggle to answer because it’s a legal battle…It’s a case between the Premier League and Manchester City that a panel will deal with.

"Am I supposed to answer that? I’m not really sure."

#1836. Dominik Szoboszlai: Liverpool handed major injury boost for Manchester United showdown after worrying footage

Dominik Szoboszlai has provided Liverpool with a big injury boost, despite playing for Hungary with heavy strapping on his right knee.

Szoboszlai’s fitness for Hungary’s Nations League double-header was up in the air at the beginning of the week after Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola admitted the midfielder was not at 100 percent.

This was after suffering a knee sprain in the 3-1 win over Crystal Palace, with Szoboszlai then linking up with his national team for further tests.

Fortunately for Liverpool - who host Manchester United in their first Premier League game after the international break - the feedback on the 26-year-old has been largely positive.

Amid worrying post-match comments and footage of Szoboszlai’s right knee being heavily strapped, he was able to complete 90 minutes of Hungary’s 2-0 win over Georgia and claimed an assist for Barnabas Varga.

"During the warm-up I was close to saying that I wouldn't be able to play after all,” Szoboszlai told reporters after the game. “I felt the injury during one of my shots.

“But I thought to myself that, having come this far, I wasn't going to let the team down. So I tried to give everything I had, as best as I could.

"My leg felt good, but now the treatment process starts all over again, and I need to be ready for Tuesday."

Hungary are next in action on Tuesday night as they host Northern Ireland in decisive final game from Nations League B, Group 2.

Szoboszlai’s side currently sit second in the table, a point behind Northern Ireland, and know they must win to gain promotion to League A.

The midfielder is likely to start in Budapest and Iraola will be hopeful the Liverpool No8 comes through the game unscathed ahead of the Man United showdown at Anfield five days later.

#1835. Mauricio Pochettino sends message to Sir Alex Ferguson ahead of Man Utd mission

Mauricio Pochettino would welcome the chance to speak with Sir Alex Ferguson as he prepares for the task of resurrecting Manchester United.

Michael Carrick’s successor’s penultimate match in charge of United States ended in an emphatic 6-0 thrashing of Haiti as he moved a step closer to beginning his United tenure.

The former Tottenham boss will start life at the Red Devils on Wednesday after two Nations League matches with Haiti, but USA all but assured their place in the semi-finals of the competition with a comprehensive first-leg showing.

Austin Trusty’s smart finish from a 10th-minute set-piece ensured Pochettino’s team were ahead at half-time before they ran riot after the break with Christian Pulisic able to net a brace either side of goals from Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun ahead of Tuesday’s second leg.

Pochettino paid tribute to his staff and players in an emotional press conference on Friday and duly watched USA romp to a 6-0 victory.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘We played for him,’ Trusty said in a post-match interview with TNT Sports after opening the scoring in the 10th minute.

‘Obviously, he’s our gaffer. Obviously it’s sad that he’s moving on. It’s a great opportunity that he’s moving on to. But we played for him. It’s his team. It’s his identity, and the mindset is to win every single game, every single match.’

The second leg of the Nations League quarterfinals will take place Tuesday in Cincinnati.

‘Pochettino is an amazing manager and he added a lot to us with the national team,’ Folarin Balogun told TNT Sports. ‘It’s always sad to see a top coach leave but it’s a part of the sport.’

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

The 54-year-old will have little time to reflect on his accomplishments in his soon-to-be former role as he will immediately begin plotting for his first game in charge of United at Anfield next Sunday.

Pochettino inherits a side that is currently in the bottom three in the Premier League table, short on confidence and a dressing room split following the recent actions of senior players, including the likes of Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martinez.

Given the current state of play and his pre-existing relationship with Ferguson, it is perhaps no surprise that Pochettino is seeking the advice of the club’s greatest ever manager as he prepares to embark on arguably the toughest assignment of his managerial career to date.

‘Not yet, but for sure I will have the opportunity after Tuesday,’ Pochettino told Telegraph Sport when asked if he had been in contact with Ferguson.

‘I said many years ago and always I say the same – for me, Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him.

‘For sure, from Tuesday, we will have the possibility to talk – if I will have time because it’s going to be very intense.

‘But if there’s the possibility to talk, then of course I will do that.’

The Metropolitano Stadium, home of La Liga giants Atletico Madrid, will stage a decisive Nations League showdown on Sunday evening as top spot in Group A3 is up for grabs.

As Spain won the reverse fixture at Wembley Stadium back in September, they just require a point to qualify for the quarter-finals as group winners.

However, due to having a superior goal difference and taking UEFA’s tiebreaker rules into account, victory in Madrid for England would see them leapfrog the reigning world and European champions.

Speaking ahead of the game, De La Fuente spoke highly of the Three Lions by saying: “These are two of world football's powerhouses. It's one of the best matches you can watch.

“Of the different styles of football, I prefer ours because our players are suited to it.

"We'll see if anyone breaks these records in the future, but for now we're on the longest-ever unbeaten run. And we're not stopping here; we want to break more records and stretch them even further."

Alex Baena, a scorer in Spain’s 3-2 win over England earlier in the season, then echoed the words of his national team manager.

He said: "I think England and us are the two best teams in the world on form. They're a great team, with a great coach, absolutely fantastic players and, on top of that, the Ballon d'Or winner."

As per FIFA’s current world rankings, Sunday’s showdown pits the team ranked top (Spain) against the team ranked fourth (England), though the next official update is expected early next week.

#1825. Manchester United: Sir Alex Ferguson has already approved of Mauricio Pochettino as talks planned

Mauricio Pochettino says he will have the opportunity to speak to Sir Alex Ferguson as his Manchester United tenure gets underway.

Pochettino was announced as the new Man United head coach on Friday, succeeding Michael Carrick who had been sacked the day before, with the club languishing in the Premier League relegation zone.

However, the Argentine has not yet officially started work at Old Trafford.

As communicated in Man Utd’s official statement, Pochettino has been allowed to finish up his commitments with the United States Men’s National Team (USMNT) and their double-header against Haiti.

The first of which took place on Saturday evening with USA recording a 6-0 win to put one foot in the CONCACAF Nations League finals.

Following Pochettino’s penultimate game in charge of USA, he spoke to the Telegraph and was asked if he can spoken to Ferguson since accepting the Man United job.

“Not yet, but for sure I will have the opportunity after Tuesday,” the 54-year-old said.

“I said many years ago and always I say the same – for me, Sir Alex Ferguson represents everything that I admire from a coach, a head coach, a man, a manager and I think he represents my values. I really admire him.

“For sure, from Tuesday, we will have the possibility to talk – if I will have time because it’s going to be very intense. But if there’s the possibility to talk, then of course I will do that.”

Pochettino and Ferguson have remained in close contact since first dining with each other in 2016.

They first crossed paths in the dugout during the 2012-13 season when Man United beat Southampton at Old Trafford, though Pochettino left a lasting impression on Ferguson despite the defeat.

"For the first 30 minutes we were fantastic," Ferguson told BBC Sport in January 2013. "But in the second half Southampton have been the best team to play here this season. We were fortunate to win."

Then in 2016, David Lammy, MP for Tottenham, shared details of a meeting with Ferguson at a charity function.

"I’m going to let you in to a secret," Lammy told The Spurs Show podcast. "About six weeks ago I sat next to Alex Ferguson at a dinner in support of grassroots football abroad.

"He said to me, 'I think you guys have the best manager in the Premier League.' Alex Ferguson said that."

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Declan Rice is "a machine", according to Bruno Guimaraes, who says he is learning a lot from his Arsenal team-mate.

Guimaraes joined Arsenal for a reported £75m from Newcastle United in August, and has shown promising signs that he is creating a strong midfield partnership with Rice.

The Brazilian has made 14 appearances in all competitions since joining Arsenal, and has made and won more tackles than any of his team-mates (15/24).

Rice, however, tops the charts for touches (1,229), assists (five), successful passes (931/1,026), and possessions won (61).

And Guimaraes was full of high praise for the England defender, who hinted he will be signing a new Arsenal deal soon.

"Look, I think that ever since he announced I was coming here, everything was practically set," Guimaraes told ESPN Brazil.

"He sent me a message right away saying: 'We've had a lot of fights in the past, but now we're friends – we're going to play together. I'm really happy you're coming here. You're going to really raise the level of our team'.

"So, he was a guy who had already won me over even before I arrived. We know – I'd say he's a complete player; he's a machine on the field.

"He can run, I don't know, 22 kilometres in a game without stopping for a second. I was really happy.

"I'm learning from him – learning a lot from him – since he's a very technical player.

"So, I think we have one of the best midfields in Europe here. Yes – given the number of players we have – and anyway, I think Declan is a guy who's been helping me a lot; I felt right at home."

"I'm happy here; I'm starting my journey here as well," Guimaraes added.

#1822. Arsenal: Why Kepa Arrizabalaga was allowed to make second international debut amid surprise twist

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga has been in action during the international break, though not for the Spain national team.

The 32-year-old, who joined the Gunners from London rivals Chelsea in July 2025 for £5million, has 13 senior caps for La Roja, but has not made an appearance since a 2-0 loss to Scotland in March 2023.

Overlooked once again by Luis de la Fuente for Spain’s Nations League double-header against the Czech Republic and England in favour of Unai Simon, Joan Garcia and Arsenal team-mate David Raya, it was set to be a quiet international window for Kepa.

In a surprise turn of events, Kepa was called up to the Basque Country squad for their friendly against Venezuela and made his debut on Saturday, playing 45 minutes of the 1-0 win at San Mames.

While Athletic Club star Mikel Jauregizar scored the only goal of the game, some Arsenal fans may have been left wondering why their back-up goalkeeper was able to play for another national team.

Of course, it is well known that FIFA rules state that players cannot switch national teams after they've played three competitive fixtures.

However, despite Kepa winning 13 senior caps for Spain, he was cleared to play for the Basque Country because they are currently not recognised by FIFA.

As such, the win over Venezuela was not an official match, in the eyes of football's governing body.

Nevertheless, Kepa was able to get valuable minutes in his legs, having made just one appearance for Arsenal so far this season - the 4-2 win over Ipswich in the Carabao Cup third round.

Future Kepa appearances for the Basque Country could be in doubt as they have started the process to secure official international status for the national team.

Part of a statement reads: “The Basque Football Federation (EFF-FVF) has revived the process to obtain international official status for the Basque National Team, both men's and women's.

“With this aim, it has approached the Supreme Sports Council and has communicated information about the initiative to the Spanish Football Federation.”

#1819. Ian Wright praises ‘magnificent’ Arsenal star after England beat Spain

Ian Wright praised ‘magnificent’ Arsenal defender Ben White after England’s thrilling Nations League win over World Cup holders Spain.

England ended Spain’s incredible 43-match unbeaten run with a 3-2 victory in Madrid on Sunday evening.

The Three Lions were bright from the start and took the lead on the stroke of half-time through a penalty from England record goalscorer and Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane.

Ezri Konsa headed in Declan Rice’s corner shortly after the interval and England were in dreamland when White added a third on the hour mark, arriving at the back-post and firing past Unai Simon.

Spain were being outplayed but had renewed hope when Elliot Anderson was sent off for bringing down Lamine Yamal as he raced through on goal and Mikel Oyarzabal converted the subsequent penalty.

England fans were having flashbacks of last summer’s World Cup semi-final collapse against Argentina when Nico Williams scored Spain’s second to set up a tense final 20 minutes.

The hosts pressed for an equaliser but were denied by some valiant England defending and an impressive display from goalkeeper James Trafford.

The hard-fought win means England, already through to the quarter-finals of the Nations League, finish top of their group ahead of World Cup holders Spain.

Wright felt England ‘deserved’ the win despite the late pressure from Spain and singled out Arsenal star White for special praise.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

White was part of England’s World Cup group in Qatar four years ago but left Gareth Southgate’s squad for personal reasons.

He then made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Southgate’s reign, a decision that has led to him being booed by some England fans in recent games.

‘Can I just say, I’m really pleased for Ben White and the way things have turned around for him,’ Wright said on ITV.

‘It’s just brilliant for him to get back in and he was magnificent tonight. Not just with the goal but he was making tackles, niggling the Spain players. I’m so pleased it’s ended that way for him.

"This England team are RUNNING RIOT in Spain" 🤩👀 They lead the World Cup winners by 3-0 in Madrid!! WOW. pic.twitter.com/2GuDnscRb4

‘There was a lot to be excited about for England. They were 3-0 up and cruising against the world champions before the red kind of changed the game.’

Meanwhile, Arsenal midfielder Rice said the England squad ‘knew’ they were going to end Spain’s two-year unbeaten run.

‘We knew we were going to beat them tonight,’ he said on ITV. ‘The message from the manager after the Croatia game has been so positive.

‘The first 10 minutes was the best we’ve played. Overall 10 men for half an hour, winning 3-2 against a team unbeaten in 43 is massive.

‘Argentina that day [at the World Cup] wasn’t meant to be. That’s football. When they [Spain] got a second maybe it could have gone another way. It’s a massive win.’

The former England captain said stopping drinking has completely overhauled his lifestyle, and that Coleen has noticed the difference in his appearance, happiness and in their relationship.

Rooney, 41, told The Mail on Sunday: “She’s obviously happy because I think, from a point of view of our marriage, it’s in a better place, in a much happier place. And so that obviously makes a difference.

#1816. Prediction: Hungary vs Northern Ireland

Everything is on the line in Budapest on Tuesday evening as Hungary and Northern Ireland meet in the decisive match of their UEFA Nations League campaign.

The visitors lead the group by a single point heading into the final round of fixtures, meaning a draw would secure promotion for Northern Ireland, while Hungary must win to leapfrog their rivals and clinch top spot.

Hungary head into the final round of Nations League group matches knowing that only a victory will be enough to secure automatic promotion to League A.

Marco Rossi’s side currently sit second in the group with 10 points, one behind leaders Northern Ireland, meaning the equation is straightforward at the Puskas Arena. A win would send the Magyars into first place and guarantee promotion, while any other result would leave them depending on a promotion playoff.

Hungary boosted their chances with a 2-0 victory over Georgia on Saturday, although they were made to work hard for the breakthrough and relied on an own goal from Lasha Dvali to open the scoring.

That success was their third consecutive Nations League win and continued a strong run of form that has seen them lose only once in their last nine matches in all competitions. During their recent three-game winning streak, Hungary have scored five goals and kept two clean sheets.

Home form has also been encouraging. The Magyars have won four of their last six matches when playing on home soil and will believe they have a genuine opportunity to overturn the one-point deficit separating them from Northern Ireland.

Dominik Szoboszlai revealed he almost suffered an injury before the victory over Georgia, but the Liverpool midfielder is expected to feature and could operate in an advanced role.

Hungary are without Milan Vitalis through suspension, while captain Willi Orban is also banned, potentially forcing Attila Szalai into the starting lineup.

Barnabas Varga is expected to lead the attack and will be aiming to score his 17th international goal.

Northern Ireland arrive in Budapest sitting at the top of the group and knowing that a draw will be enough to secure promotion to League A for the first time.

Michael O’Neill’s side strengthened their position with a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Ukraine on Saturday, courtesy of a long-range strike from Terry Devlin. That result moved them onto 11 points and left them in control of their own destiny heading into the final matchday.

The Green and White Army have become extremely difficult to beat. Their only defeat in their last eight matches came against France in June, with four wins and three draws recorded during that period.

While Northern Ireland have not always been prolific, they have consistently found ways to collect results. They have scored exactly one goal in five of their last eight games and have developed a reputation for staying competitive in tight contests.

Their record against Hungary is reasonably encouraging too. Northern Ireland have only lost one of the last four meetings between the nations and held Hungary to a goalless draw earlier in the group stage.

The visitors have also won both of their away fixtures in this Nations League campaign, although their broader away record remains mixed.

Jamie Donley will miss the game after picking up a yellow card against Ukraine.

His absence could see Josh Magennis lead the attack, with Ethan Galbraith and Isaac Price expected to provide support from wide areas.

Shea Charles should once again be tasked with controlling the midfield.

This is effectively a winner-takes-all contest for automatic promotion, although Northern Ireland hold the advantage of knowing that a draw will achieve their objective.

Hungary’s recent form and strong home record make them slight favourites to claim victory, but Northern Ireland have built their campaign on defensive resilience and consistency. The visitors have proved extremely difficult to break down throughout the group and already held Hungary scoreless earlier in the campaign.

With the stakes so high and neither side likely to take unnecessary risks, a closely contested encounter seems to be on the cards, and the visitors are likely to leave with what they come for: a point.

Prediction: Austria vs Republic of Ireland

#1815. Romano and Moretto provide update on Milan’s Endrick pursuit: “Hasn’t said no”

This week, there have been some interesting rumours about AC Milan and their pursuit of Endrick. However, it may have been a bit misleading.

Yesterday, it seemed that Milan were almost out of the race to sign Endrick, with the Brazilian against the club’s Devil logo. Instead, the Corriere dello Sport report would have you believe that he’d prefer a move to Roma.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, his agency have denied this rumour and later reports suggested that the Rossoneri are very much in the race to sign the Brazilian. In fact, he could even leave Real Madrid permanently – with future clauses – so things have certainly developed a bit this week.

Speaking on his YouTube channel today, Romano provided an update on Endrick’s situation alongside Matteo Moretto and their words have been relayed by MilanNews.

“Endrick is currently evaluating his future. On one side, Real Madrid doesn’t want to release him, from the president to Jose Mourinho, who continues to reiterate this publicly; on the other, the boy wants to play,” Romano started.

“I wanted to add a footnote: Endrick’s entourage, ROC Nation, are letting it be known that the player hasn’t said no to Milan; he hasn’t said no to anyone on November 12th. He’s still in the evaluation phase; we’ll see what happens.

“He has two months left with Real Madrid: football changes in five minutes. Endrick’s position is currently completely open, and he’s a player—we were the first to talk about him—that Milan really likes. But it’s true that Roma is also there, there’s a queue of many teams ready to chase him.

“I just wanted to clarify that Endrick hasn’t said no to Milan. He’s keeping everything open while waiting to figure out—if he leaves—the best solution.”

Moretto then added, “A lot will depend on the player. In December, he’ll really understand what kind of path he wants to take. He’s currently noticing this lack of playing time, so the loan option is taking shape. Roma have been maintaining contact for weeks.

“Roma want an additional striker because they believe with one or two signings they can really compete for something important this year. Keep an eye on Roma, but Milan was one of the first to move, and the relationship between Cardinale and ROC Nation is excellent. So far, Roma has maintained contact a little more actively, but Milan is insisting.”

It’s clear that January will be very interesting where Endrick is involved, especially with him being the one to make the decisions on his future.

#1811. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1810. Low: Germany moving in positive direction under Klopp

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Joachim Low believes Jurgen Klopp is moving Germany in a "positive direction", though he warned that there will be setbacks for the team.

Klopp replaced Julian Nagelsmann as Germany's head coach following their shock World Cup last-32 exit at the hands of Paraguay on penalties.

He has overseen five games so far in the Nations League, with the team still in with a chance of reaching the quarter-finals, though their fate is going down to a final-day clash with the Netherlands in Group A2.

Klopp has won two of his games so far (D2 L1), and Germany are unbeaten in their last three outings following a 3-1 win over nine-man Serbia last time out.

Low, who led Germany to World Cup glory in 2014, has so far been impressed by what he has seen from Klopp's start.

"He is doing a very, very good job," Low told Bild TV.

"He gives the players a lot of confidence and is trying to develop a sustainable playing philosophy.

"You get the feeling that things are heading in a positive direction."

Klopp has already faced bumps along the way, failing to win either of his first two matches, including a shock 1-0 loss to Greece.

But in recent years, Germany have struggled to go toe-to-toe with the best; at World Cups, they have fallen at the group stage twice since their 2014 triumph, while this year's exit came at the first hurdle of the knockout stages.

And Low urged caution against raising expectations too high this early into Klopp's reign.

"His name alone does not always guarantee success. There will still be a few setbacks before we get back to that level," Low added.

"The results are not all that important at this stage. We are in the Nations League now, and qualifying begins next year, which we will get through.

"The important thing will be for the team to spend six months playing together and building an understanding.

"You cannot expect any coach to get everything working within a few weeks. You have to look at whether there is progress."

Germany face the Netherlands in their final Nations League game on Monday, knowing a win will take them into the last eight of the tournament.

#1809. How Thomas Tuchel instilled winning England instinct to secure historic victory over Spain

When Thomas Tuchel and his England coaching staff come to reflect on England’s sensational victory in Spain, they will come to the conclusion it could scarcely have gone better.

Such a statement may feel bizarre given the visitors were at one stage 3-0 up with cruise control applied, before another Jarell Quansah error led to an Elliot Anderson red card, a penalty converted, and then a second goal back for a Spain team totally rejuvenated.

The reality, though, is that if England’s canter to a one-sided victory had continued as it was doing, Tuchel and his team would have far less to pore over as they unpick the headers and volleys at the end of this calendar year and the learning they can take from what still finished - by getting over the line 3-2 and topping the group — a hugely successful international break.

Tuchel had repeatedly described this affair as “a final” in the days leading up, but just as important as finishing top of the group and the potentially easier quarter-final opponent it could secure them in March was delivering a performance to provide encouragement that the Three Lions can indeed go toe-to-toe with the very best and avoid unforced errors in the process.

OK, there was one such mistake: Quansah, at fault for Croatia’s goal at Wembley on Thursday, dawdling on the ball and conceding the ball cheaply. England’s magnificent earlier work threatened to unravel at that point as the dominoes of the resultant penalty a red card and goal and second goal fell.

But then came the memories of the cavalry this summer, their resolute World Cup closing-it-out jobs against Mexico and then Norway and then the ugly attempt to do it all over again at the semi-final against Argentina. Instinct kicked in.

James Trafford getting the nod ahead of Jordan Pickford in the Spanish capital was a bold call, as was Ben White starting at right-back and Lewis Hall on the left, but all three were superb, as the head coach’s big decisions were wholly vindicated. The world champions’ 43-game winning run was ended by England, the Spanish tasting defeat in Madrid for the first time in 39 years, since a certain Gary Lineker netted all four in a 4-2 England win.

Lamine Yamal posed England all sorts of questions from the right wing - a fabulous player - but did he cause them a wealth of problems? Aside from a simple assist for Spain’s second, no, not really. Hall was sturdy at left-back, just as England were all over the pitch.

Their first-half display, after which point they led 1-0 through a Harry Kane penalty, was described by Roy Keane in ITV’s coverage as “perfect”. They had certainly all been on the same wavelength, their passing sequences all crisp. And in the second half, after those two quickfire goals shipped, the defensive equivalent of that joined-up thinking was visible from a team that looked like one.

The players involved in this Nations League group game represent many of the Champions League powerhouses and yet there was no hint of this being an unwanted match that disrupts the club football juggernaut and where there is a needless risk of injury. Not a bit of that. When Jude Bellingham’s number came up and he was substituted in the 83rd minute, presumably to keep Real Madrid happy, he looked angered not to be carrying on in a game that had just about everything. What’s more: it had the result that England craved. And expected.

“We knew we were going to beat them tonight,” said Declan Rice. Not only a thrilling night for England, it will also have taught them plenty about themselves. That is just as important.

#1806. FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

Home » Home 2 » FIFA Slaps Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid With 1-Year Transfer Bans

The ban will start from the July transfer window this year and finish with the January transfer market in 2017.

Atletico were also fined 900,000 Swiss francs (820,000 euros) and Real 360,000 (330,000 euros).

“The two clubs were found to have violated several provisions concerning the international transfer and first registration of minor players as well as other relevant provisions with regard to the registration and participation of certain players in competitions,” said a FIFA statement.

Barcelona has just ended a one year ban for similar reasons.

Real and Atletico were “issued with a reprimand and given 90 days in which to regularise the situation of all minor players concerned,” FIFA said. They can still sell players during the transfer ban.

FIFA said the alarm was raised over the two clubs by FIFA’s Transfer Matching System and its disciplinary committee completed the inquiry.

Under international football rules, players under 18 cannot be transferred to another country, except in limited circumstances. All transfers need the approval of a special FIFA committee.

“The investigations concerned minor players who were involved and participated in competitions with the clubs over various periods between 2007 and 2014 (Atletico Madrid) and between 2005 and 2014 (Real Madrid),” FIFA said.

The ban follows a similar sanction handed to European champions Barcelona, who were unable to register new players during 2015.

Barca were initially banned in April 2014, but managed to delay the sanction taking affect until the transfer windows in January and the summer 2015 by launching an ultimately unsuccessful appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

By delaying the ban, Barca managed to sign the likes of Luis Suarez and Ivan Rakitic in the summer of 2014 to propel them to a treble of La Liga, Champions League and Copa del Rey.

The news is just the latest institutional embarassment for Real Madrid just over a week after they appointed French legend Zinedine Zidane.

Madrid have sacked two Champions League winning coaches in Carlo Ancelotti and Rafael Benitez in the past seven months, as well as being thrown out of the Copa del Rey for fielding an ineligible player.

The sanction could also be bad news for the likes of Paris Saint-Germain and Manchester United, who had targeted Madrid stars Cristiano Ronaldo and Gareth Bale with Real highly unlikely to dispose of their best players without the chance to sign suitable replacements.

La Liga leaders Atletico Madrid’s usually hectic transfer policy will also be put on hold. However, Diego Simeone’s men look better placed to cope with the ban having invested heavily in young talent over the past year.

Neither Real no Atletico made an immediate comment on whether they would appeal.

#1804. Xavi: Netherlands players out to enjoy themselves in huge Germany test

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Netherlands coach Xavi wants his team to go out and enjoy themselves when they take on Germany, though he knows Jurgen Klopp's team will pose a huge challenge.

The Oranje turned in their best display under Xavi yet last time out, as they hammered Greece 7-0.

That victory sent the Netherlands to the top of Nations League Group A2 on 11 points, three better off than third-place Germany, who beat Serbia 3-1. Greece sit second, also on eight points.

With Germany and the Netherlands having drawn on MD1, it means the winner of Monday's game will go through to the quarter-finals, though a point for the Oranje would be enough.

If Germany win, then the Netherlands will still go through if Serbia avoid defeat against Greece.

And Xavi has asked his players to go out with the same level of enjoyment that they had during their rout of Greece on Friday.

A Donyell Malen special! https://t.co/hnzMJGY7mZ

— OnsOranje (@OnsOranje) November 15, 2026

"The players enjoyed themselves against Greece and they want to do that again against Germany," Xavi told reporters.

"I am so proud of them. I am convinced that they can be good again. We know how it should be done. We need to bring in even more continuity.

"Now that I am [the] coach, I feel the rivalry [with Germany]. That is why it is so important for us. It is a fantastic test."

Germany's win over Serbia was just their second victory under Jurgen Klopp, who is out to avoid an underwhelming start to his tenure.

"It is difficult to surprise other coaches, and certainly Jurgen Klopp. He is one of the best coaches of recent years," Xavi said.

"It will be a big challenge. They have to win. It is a big test."

The Netherlands have not won any of their last five meetings against Germany, with their last victory coming in a Euro 2020 qualifier in September 2019 (4-2).

But there was also a long-term vision in place. Liverpool's mission isn't to immediately claw their way back to the top. The club understands that rebuilding takes time.

Ward will be granted that time, and he should be trusted to be a much more savvy recruiter and negotiators in comparison to Hughes.

Liverpool's next steps under Ward are clearThere are certain areas that have been identified as problematic for Ward and his department. Milos Kerkez also needs competition in the left-back spot. Kostas Tsimikas just simply isn't at the level capable of pushing the Hungarian to greater heights. There's also the midfield. Liverpool have options there but it is moot whether those are the right options for Andoni Iraola's style of play. #1799. EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Home » Home 2 » EPL Prepares for Most Exciting Title Race in Years

Now that all of the top four English Premier League teams have had a chance to play each other, we find ourselves looking at one of the most wide open title races in recent memory. As of this writing, the league leaders are only separated by a mere six points. With the exception of Manchester City, we could very well see a new face hoisting the Premier League trophy at the end of the season.

For much of the year, it looked like Arsenal would be in the running for its first league title in more than a decade. With the Gunners’ recent victory against Leicester City, they are very much back in the conversation. Danny Welbeck returned to the pitch for the first time this season and made an immediate impact for Arsene Wenger’s squad, scoring the last-minute, game-winning goal to propel the team to within two points of the top spot. Given that even more key players are set to return to action for Arsenal in the coming months, this is easily the best shot they have had of winning a championship since their undefeated 2003-04 season.

Another surprise team that certainly deserves its own mention is Tottenham Hotspur. Following the club’s controversial defeat of Manchester City, the Spurs sit in second place, a mere two points behind Leicester City and ahead of Arsenal on goal differential. Tottenham have yet to win a title in the Premier League era and they have not won an English championship since 1961. The team has done a superb job of backing up star striker Harry Kane with a glut of promising young players, and their goal tally only helps to reinforce the wisdom behind the strategy of manager Mauricio Pochettino.

Meanwhile, Manchester City is still hoping to snag its third title as something of a swan song for exiting manager Manuel Pellegrini. It was recently announced that the club had hired Pep Guardiola . from Bayern Munich to take charge of the team beginning with next season. Thus, Pellegrini has been forced to endure the rest of the campaign as a dead man walking. Despite the impending exit of Pellegrini, City are still in the race for the Premier League title in addition to both the F.A. Cup and Champions League. Theoretically, the club could pull off a treble, if it can manage a solid string of performances during the final half of the season.

At the beginning of the season, it was expected that the usual suspects would once again dominate the league. Many predicted the reigning champs at Chelsea to repeat their success. However, a shocking season has seen the team part ways with controversial manager Jose Mourinho and struggle to remain in the top half of the tables with hopes of a Champions League spot dashed long ago.

For the first time in years, there’s a chance to see a completely new team win the league. No matter which club you support, there’s no denying that this has made for one of the most thrilling contests in recent memory. In a league where money talks, small fish like Leicester City are surprising everyone, and we can only hope that this means a new era of parity for the Premier League.

#1798. Mauricio Pochettino faces grim Man United relegation statistic

By Naim Beneddra | 14 Nov 2026 11:33

Mauricio Pochettino will inherit a Manchester United side facing a worrying historical relegation precedent, with 41.5% of Premier League teams who collected eight points from their opening 10 matches ultimately going down.

The Argentine was confirmed as United's new head coach on Friday, replacing Michael Carrick after a disastrous start to the 2026-27 campaign left the Red Devils 18th in the Premier League.

United have managed just one victory in their opening 10 league fixtures, collecting eight points despite finishing third last season and returning to the Champions League.

According to an analysis published by Opta Analyst on November 10, 41 teams have recorded exactly eight points after 10 Premier League games since the competition's creation in 1992.

Of those, 17 were relegated at the end of the season, representing a rate of 41.5%.

The figures underline the scale of Pochettino's challenge, although the historical percentage should not be confused with United's actual probability of relegation this season.

1 - Manchester United's eight points after 10 games are their fewest in a league season at this stage since 1986-87 (also eight), the season Alex Ferguson arrived as manager in November. Poch? https://t.co/hvyVWQ2vja

Opta's research offers a sobering comparison for a club that has not played outside the English top flight since the 1974-75 season.

Of the 10 most recent teams to collect exactly eight points from their opening 10 Premier League matches, four were subsequently relegated.

Southampton suffered that fate in 2022-23, finishing bottom with 25 points, while Swansea City went down in 2017-18 after collecting 33 points.

Norwich City in 2013-14 and Wolverhampton Wanderers in 2011-12 also failed to recover from similarly poor starts.

There is some encouragement for United, with the other 24 clubs in the wider historical sample ultimately retaining their Premier League status.

Nevertheless, the latest Opta supercomputer projections before Carrick's dismissal suggested that United's risk of relegation had risen substantially.

The model gave the Red Devils a 20.9% chance of going down, compared with just 3.6% before the season began.

That represents almost a sixfold increase, although the simulations were conducted before Pochettino's appointment and do not account for any potential improvement under the new manager.

United's underlying results offer little reassurance.

They have scored 14 league goals but conceded 19, leaving them with a goal difference of minus five. Their dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last weekend, rescued by two stoppage-time goals, was another illustration of their defensive difficulties.

The club's current position also carries historical significance.

Before this month, United had not ended a day in the relegation zone beyond August since October 1986, shortly before Sir Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson.

They spent 28 consecutive days in the bottom three during that campaign, eventually finishing 11th in Ferguson's first season.

With the international break keeping United out of action until November 22, their current spell in the relegation zone is guaranteed to last at least 15 days, their longest such run since 1986.

Pochettino's appointment has offered United a potential turning point, but the 54-year-old faces an exceptionally demanding introduction.

The former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager will officially take charge on November 18 after completing his remaining commitments with the United States national team.

His first match will be against Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, November 22, leaving him little time to work with his new squad.

United could even begin that fixture at the bottom of the Premier League, depending on results involving Sunderland and Crystal Palace earlier in the weekend.

More significantly, remaining in the relegation zone after the 11th round of fixtures would represent another unwanted milestone.

According to Opta, United have not occupied a relegation position this late into a top-flight season since November 1986, when Ferguson was beginning his legendary managerial tenure.

Pochettino will therefore have an immediate opportunity to change the direction of United's campaign, although his appointment has already raised questions about the scale of the rebuilding task.

The Argentine arrives with a reputation for developing young players and building aggressive, high-intensity teams, qualities United highlighted when announcing his appointment.

However, the immediate priority will be restoring defensive stability and converting the team's attacking output into victories.

United have another 28 Premier League matches remaining, giving their new manager sufficient time to move the club away from danger.

The historical numbers provide a reminder of how damaging their opening 10 games have been, but the more immediate challenge is clear: Pochettino must deliver an improvement quickly enough to prevent a difficult start from becoming a genuine relegation battle.

Mauricio Pochettino will stay in charge of the USA's upcoming international games instead of joining up with Man United

#1795. The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

Home » Home 2 » The Rock of London: Looking back at John Terry’s Chelsea FC career

At the start of this season, John Terry leaving Chelsea was the last thing on anyone’s mind. All was rosy at Stamford Bridge, the home of the newly crowed English champions. In over 21 years at the club, there was no indication that Terry would not retire a Chelsea man.

The Blues’ skipper’s announcement in January 2016, then, came as a shock to the Chelsea faithful, bringing notice to the seemingly premature — even if inevitable — fall of the curtain on a legendary career.

After making his debut in the League Cup against Aston Villa late in 1998, John Terry made sporadic appearances under Gianluca Vialli, before joining Nottingham Forest on a short loan spell. He broke into the first team in 2000-01, when manager Claudio Ranieri handed him 22 Premier League appearances during a season that the 20-year-old would finish as the club’s Player of the Year.

It would be the first of several achievements to come.

Terry’s importance to the team grew as Ranieri relied on his partnership with then-captain Marcel Desailly to mastermind Chelsea’s progression from a fashionable mid-table club to a Champions League team that meant business. They received a major shot in the arm when Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich bought the club in 2003. It was also a significant year in Terry’s international career as he made his England debut against Serbia and Montenegro in June.

The season that followed saw Chelsea finish above perennial winners Manchester United for the first time in Premier League history, and defeat Premiership invincibles Arsenal en route to the club’s first Champions League semifinal. Terry ended the season making a first of four appearances in the PFA Team of the Year, and went to Portugal for the European Championships having displaced Sol Campbell as England’s first choice centre-back.

In the summer of 2004, Chelsea brought in Jose Mourinho, who was fresh from winning a treble with the unfancied FC Porto and raring to take on bigger challenges. The 23-year-old Terry was named captain as Chelsea embarked on the most successful period in the club’s history. In the three seasons that followed, Chelsea won 2 league cups, 2 Premier League titles and the FA Cup — success built on a core of John Terry, Frank Lampard, Petr Cech and Didier Drogba, Chelsea’s ‘old guard’.

This was also a period when Terry picked up several individual accolades. He was named PFA Player of the Year in 2005, the first defender to win the award since Paul McGrath in 1993. He would make a first of five consecutive appearances in the FIFPro World XI in 2005, as well as a first of four appearances in the UEFA Team of the Year.

He was also voted Chelsea’s Player of the Year for the second time in his career in 2006. Steve McClaren, hired as England manager after an underwhelming 2006 World Cup, named the Chelsea skipper as England captain.

Terry was now, beyond argument, one of football’s best.

However, more testing times were to come.

September 2007 saw the departure of Mourinho after a falling out with the club board. The season itself promised much but left a Chelsea squad dejected on three occasions as they saw the League Cup, the Premier League and the Champions League trophies go elsewhere.

For the European Cup in particular, Terry was left with no one but himself to blame as he slipped for the crucial penalty, a moment he has said will haunt him forever. Chelsea and Terry experienced further European heartbreak the following season as Tom Henning Ovrebo had a refereeing performance to forget at Stamford Bridge, handing Barcelona a berth in the final and eventually the trophy.

In early 2010, when he was revealed as the English footballer who had an affair with Vanessa Perroncel, Wayne Bridge’s ex-girlfriend — a horrendous personal error that cost him his status as England captain — it made him the perennial recipient of passionate booing across English grounds. After the revelation, Chelsea travelled to Burnley. Amidst a frosty reception, he scored a late winner to put Carlo Ancelotti’s side back on track in the title race, one they would go on to win in some style. All of this typified John Terry — imperfect, but unshakeable.

Terry had built an unflappable reputation as a top class defender, leader and hard man. He said about himself, “I still say if the ball is there to be won I will go for it, whether with my head or whatever, and if it means us scoring or stopping a goal, I won’t think twice.”

The period that followed, however, was not good for Chelsea or their captain. The team finished the 2010-11 season trophyless, and Carlo Ancelotti paid for it with his job. This was the first of two times in Terry’s career where he and his club would have an extremely underwhelming season following a dominant one, and it also marked the first attempt to phase him out of the first team.

New manager Andre Villas-Boas attempted to introduce a high defensive line that left Terry exposed on a number of occasions, and saw the young Portuguese manager fall back on quicker defenders to implement his system. He was also determined to make lesser use of Frank Lampard and displace Didier Drogba with Fernando Torres. These were unpopular moves that led to poor results and eventually his sacking. Terry was not helped by another personal abberation, mouthing racial profanity at Anton Ferdinand of QPR, an act that saw him land a lengthy ban and damage his position in the England squad almost beyond repair.

Interim manager Roberto Di Matteo reinstated the old guard, and was rewarded with the ultimate prize — the first Champions League in Chelsea’s history.

Terry retired from international football following EURO 2012, leaving him to focus on his club career. However, further rotation was to follow during the reign of Rafael Benitez, who played Terry only in games of lesser importance. This was something he could do with relative impunity owing to the fact that his stock could not have fallen any further among Chelsea fans.

The writing was seemingly on the wall, however. Unsavoury incidents were fresher in the memory than individual accolades, the skipper was out of favour for two seasons running, and was well over 30 years of age. Was John Terry done?

Mourinho did not share the views of Benitez and Villas-Boas. Where they saw a slowing, easily-exposed has-been, he saw an experienced warrior with an excellent reading of the game who could form a title-winning partnership with the quicker Gary Cahill.

Terry grabbed the opportunity he was handed with gusto, performing with excellence in Mourinho’s lower defensive block. The English pair formed the core of a defence that would go on to win the club’s fourth Premier League title in 2015, leading the table from the opening day to the end. It was a landmark achievement for Terry in particular as he played every minute of a league campaign for the first time in his career, aged 34.

Once again they tried to put him down. Once again he fed off it and rose tall.

Chelsea did not start the defence of their title well at all, gathering just 4 points from the first 4 matches. Mourinho, who asked Terry to take the club on his shoulders in 2004 and stood by him for two seasons in his second stint, hauled off his skipper at half-time at the Etihad in the second game of the season, and began to rotate him out of the team, giving an increasing number of starts to the young Kurt Zouma.

The season did not take much of a turn for the better even under interim manager Guus Hiddink, particularly in a defensive sense as the Blues continued to let in goals during a meek climb to the top half of the table, with or without Terry in the side.

A sending off at the Stadium of Light following an injury layoff is not the kind of ending that the fans desired for their beloved captain, who has emerged from the dugout 703 times in Chelsea colours and has been the face of the club through the most successful period in their history.

Offered a new deal by the club last week, the skipper responded, “The contract extension the club has offered me is a different role and I hope everyone will understand I want to take the time to consider it carefully before making a decision.” While fans will hope — for reasons emotional as well as those to do with football — that Terry stays on, the chances look slim.

Should the captain leave the ship, the Blues supporters’ emotions are best summed up by a certain banner that embellishes the Shed End: Captain, Leader, Legend.

#1793. Faroe Islands vs Moldova - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 14 Nov 2026 11:45

However, the visitors only require a draw to ensure that they qualify for the promotion playoffs.

Moldova head into this fixture having failed to keep a clean sheet in 20 matches, their last shutout coming in Andorra two years to the day of this game.

Meanwhile, Faroe Islands possess the unusual record of posting five successive draws in this group.

Eydun Klakstein's side now have the opportunity to secure a place in the promotion playoffs with a win on Monday.

Meanwhile, Croatia are the only nation to beat Faroe Islands in Torshavn in more than three years.

Faroe Islands will make a change at right wing-back, a consequence of Joannes Danielsen serving a one-match ban.

Jann Benjaminsen is in line to deputise in that role, while the likes of Poul Kallsberg, Joannes Bjartalid and Adrian Justinussen are alternatives having been introduced as substitutes in Slovakia.

Meanwhile, Moldova centre-back Iurie Iovu is suspended for this contest, which should lead to Mihail Stefan starting in the back three.

However, captain Vladyslav Baboglo will be assessed after being withdrawn during the latter stages versus Kazakhstan.

Petru Popescu scored both goals against Kazakhstan, taking him to four goals in nine games for the national team.

#1792. CF: Instalments and repeatable bonuses – the exact figure Milan paid for Goncalo Ramos

Today, more information about the structure and cost of Goncalo Ramos’ move to AC Milan has been revealed.

It’s fair to say that Ramos’ start to life with Milan has been poor. The Portuguese striker has not scored (or assisted) as many as had been hoped from a player worth a substantial amount and it’s fair to suggest that some have been disappointed with his time at San Siro so far.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

However, the club will not be giving up on him anytime soon, considering he is their record arrival.

This evening, Calcio e Finanza have looked at the fee paid for Ramos – as they did for Diego Moreira recently – and picked apart both the fee, the bonuses and the structure of the payment, as MilanNews relays.

In terms of the fixed fee, the Rossoneri agreed on a deal worth €70 million, with an extra €3.1m in additional costs. This figure will be paid over the course of four years, with yearly payments scheduled on July 15 on each year – ending in July 2029 – and each payment will be worth €17.5m.

Then, there is €16m in bonuses that can be achieved, taking the total fee to almost €90m if all bonuses are achieved.

If Milan win the Scudetto, €2m will be owed; then there are several Champions League bonuses, which could be worth up to €5.2m if the Diavolo win the competition. Finally, if he is the top goalscorer in Serie A, another €2m will be owed to PSG.

These bonuses are capped at €16m and are repeatable, but they’ll only be redeemable if the Portuguese plays 60% of games in that season, unless he is the top scorer, where only the €2m will be owed.

#1791. Insider confirms Liverpool sent scouts to watch Bundesliga wonderkid in action

Liverpool have thrown themselves into a lot of different deals over the last couple of years.

And, despite this, questions are still being asked about whether their first-team squad have what it takes to challenge for silverware.

Right now, it doesn't really feel like they do but, when you look at Liverpool's players, it's clear that they should.

The last few transfer windows have led to the Reds spending well over £600 million on trying to improve their ranks.

For some positions, this money has been well spent but, in others, it doesn't really feel like Liverpool have upgraded them.

Despite this, they're still on the lookout for new talent with a fresh update from Germany now confirming that.

Liverpool have sent their scouts to watch Finn Jeltsch in action

Ronald Araujo and Jeremy Jacquet may have been brought in over the summer to try and upgrade Liverpool's defence but, with all the change that is expected to come in July next year, even more defenders may need to be brought in.

Several options have already arisen as options for Andoni Iraola and Julian Ward but, none of these links have turned into concrete interest yet.

But, with Virgil van Dijk, Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas all on the verge of exiting L4, it's unclear what's actually going to happen.

If all three of them leave then another defensive rebuild will need to be carried out but, if only one or even two of them chooses to pack their bags, that might not need to happen.

Despite this, options for the upcoming summer transfer window have been entering the rumour mill each day and now, according to Bayern Munich insider Christian Falk, Finn Jeltsch has already been scouted by Liverpool in person.

"It is TRUE: Liverpool have scouted VfB Stuttgart centre-back Finn Jeltsch. All the top clubs, including Bayern Munich, are scouting him," he wrote.

"He was in the squad for Klopp first as a backup for the right-back. Then one of the central defenders became injured, and now he’s also the backup at centre-back.

"This shows he can play many positions, and everyone can see the 20-year-old’s potential. Such players really are a present to everyone. Jeltsch is young, talented and can play many positions, and he’s not so expensive!"

Finn Jeltsch ticks a lot of boxes for Liverpool

One of the main things that Liverpool have wanted from their transfers recently is players with potential.

Ever since Jurgen Klopp took over, the Reds have been in the business of using youngsters as a regular part of their first-team plans.

Obviously, Arne Slot went a bit against this and forced a lot of the Reds' young talent out of Anfield but more often than not, the Reds have always had a younger player within their starting XI.

And, since players are now going for ridiculous fees, the best way for team to sign top talent is to prise them away from their clubs while they're still young and fairly unproven.

That's why this transfer of Jeltsch ticks a lot of boxes for Liverpool. He's one of VfB Stuttgart's best players despite only being 20 years old and, even though his natural position is at centre-back, he can also be used as a right-back if needed.

He's basically a younger, and much cheaper version of Araujo which, after his performances this season, should certainly pique the interest of Liverpool's fans.

Regardless of their success, Yakin will want to see his side remain unbeaten across the entire group stage and secure another three points against Scotland on Monday.

The hosts have already proven their dominance over Scotland in the reverse fixture, winning 3-0 at Hampden Park on matchday two - marking one of four clean sheets they have recorded in the group stage.

Switzerland have also been particularly dangerous going forward, scoring 11 goals in their five matches, although they did fail to find the net for the first time in a 0-0 draw with Slovenia earlier in the November international break.

Scotland, meanwhile, head into Monday's encounter with plenty more at stake, as Sebastien Pocognoli's side remain in the race to secure a second-placed finish and the chance to earn promotion to League A.

Scotland have also remained undefeated on the road in League B Group 1 so far, recording one win and one draw, keeping back-to-back clean sheets.

Scotland also boast a better record in this fixture than Switzerland, winning eight and losing six of their 18 encounters, although they have failed to win any of their last three clashes.

Switzerland are without Johan Manzambi after the midfielder left the squad due to a calf issue, meaning Fabian Rieder is likely to start in attacking midfield once again.

After failing to score against Slovenia, Yakin could make changes elsewhere in attack, meaning Dan Ndoye and Breel Embolo could be joined by Zeki Amdouni.

Further back, Denis Zakaria and Remo Freuler should remain at the base of midfield, with Manuel Akanji and Nico Elvedi in central defence.

As for Scotland, after securing an important 2-1 win against North Macedonia, Pocognoli could name an unchanged starting 11 against Switzerland.

John McGinn scored a brace in that game, and the attacking midfielder could continue alongside Scott McTominay and behind Che Adams in the front three.

#1784. Report: Liverpool face battle with Champions League winners for star man

Liverpool are currently fourth in the Premier League table.

In any other year, this would be a decent return for the Reds, especially since we're only 10 games into the season.

However, this time around, it's far from ideal. The Anfield outfit finished fifth last season which resulted in Arne Slot being relieved of his duties.

So, with the arrival of Iraola, fans were expecting a major improvement, especially with the extra £150 million he spent on bringing more players in.

This topsy-turvy form has led fans to ask the Reds to add some fresh talent to their ranks in January but, it has also caused interest from other clubs in Liverpool's players to emerge.

Liverpool have a lot of tough decisions to make over the next few weeks.

The January transfer window is now just around the corner and Liverpool have a handful of players who's contracts are set to expire in June 2027.

This means that, by the time January comes around, all of those players will be able to speak to clubs outside of England about a free transfer.

There are many big-named players on the chopping block but, the departure that would affect Liverpool the most is Virgil van Dijk.

He's been the heart of Liverpool's defence for as long as anyone can remember so, the fact that Barcelona are now wanting to sign him is massively concerning.

"As Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk enters the final months of his contract, the 35-year-old Dutch centre-back is attracting strong interest from Barcelona, Trabzonspor, AC Milan, and Juventus," Ekrem Konur wrote.

"Available on a potential free transfer, Europe's heavyweights are circling for a world-class defensive leader, while Trabzonspor are also positioning themselves to push for a sensational Bosman move.

"All eyes are on Anfield's contract decision as Van Dijk weighs up the next major chapter of his career."

Liverpool can't let Virgil van Dijk join Barcelona

The Dutchman only has around seven months left on his deal and, since no talks have been held between Liverpool and their captain yet, some major concerns are starting to emerge.

The fact that Barcelona are even interested in signing Van Dijk should prove to everyone at Anfield that there is still an elite player within him.

To be fair, his performances from this season alone could tell anyone that.

Obviously, with this level of club interested in signing Van Dijk, Liverpool are going to have a battle on their hands to keep him at Anfield.

Talks about how long the contract will be, whether he's going to be a regular starter and whether his fitness levels are where they need to be will probably dominate conversations.

But for now, the Reds just need to make their mind up about who they want to keep before it's too late.
